Physical leaf p279 (printed page 264) and facing English leaf p280 (printed page 265) conclude the Royal Hours of the Nativity. At the Third Hour (§ 3 concl.), the Second Canonarch proclaims the Prophecy (Baruch 3:35–4:4, Christ appearing upon earth and conversing with men) and the Epistle (Galatians 3:23–29, the Law as tutor unto Christ, and adoption as sons through faith), and the Priest reads the Gospel (Luke 2:1–20, the Caesar Augustus census, the manger, and the Angelic Gloria heard by the shepherds). At the Sixth Hour (§ 4), after Psalms 71, 131, and 90 LXX, the idiomela are *Δεῦτε πιστοὶ ἐπαρθῶμεν ἐνθέως* ("Come, ye faithful, let us be inspired divinely"), *Ἄκουε, οὐρανέ* ("Hear, O heaven, and give ear, O earth"), and *Δεῦτε, χριστοφόροι λαοί* ("Come, ye Christ-bearing peoples"); the Prophecy is Isaiah 7:10–16; 8:1–4, 9–10 (the virgin conceiving Emmanuel), the Epistle is Hebrews 2:11–18 (Christ partaking of flesh and blood to destroy the devil), and the Gospel is Matthew 2:1–12 (the Adoration of the Magi). At the Ninth Hour (§ 5), after Psalms 109, 110, and 85 LXX, the idiomela are *Ἐξεπλήττετο ὁ Ἡρώδης* ("Herod was struck with amazement") and *Ὅτε Ἰωσήφ, Παρθένε* ("When Joseph, O Virgin"); then the Canonarch stands in the midst of the nave facing east and solemnly chants the celebrated idiomelon *Σήμερον γεννᾶται ἐκ Παρθένου ὁ δρακὶ τὴν πᾶσαν ἔχων κτίσιν* ("Today He Who holds all creation in the hollow of His hand is born of a Virgin") in Gospel recitative style thrice, continuing with the strophes, repeating thrice *Προσκυνοῦμέν σου τὴν γέννησιν, Χριστέ* ("We worship Thy Nativity, O Christ"), and once *Δεῖξον ἡμῖν καὶ τὰ θεῖά σου Θεοφάνεια* ("Show us also Thy divine Theophany"), whereupon the choirs repeat the idiomelon melodiously; the Prophecy is Isaiah 9:6–7 (Unto us a Child is born), the Epistle is Hebrews 2:1–10 (Jesus crowned with glory and honor), and the Gospel is Matthew 2:13–23 (the Flight into Egypt and Slaughter of the Holy Innocents). In Note 3, Violakis explains that historically the Typika were read after the Ninth Hour, but in modern practice are omitted to transition directly to Great Vespers with the Liturgy of Saint Basil the Great.

On Monday evening and Tuesday morning (Dec 25–26, § 36), Vespers, Matins, and Divine Liturgy for the Synaxis of the Most Holy Theotokos are celebrated as prescribed in Situation One §§ 9–10; the Epistle is Hebrews 2:11–18 (*Ὁ ἁγιάζων καὶ οἱ ἁγιαζόμενοι* / "Both He that sanctifieth and they who are sanctified are all of one"), and the Gospel is Matthew 2:13–23 (*Ἀναχωρησάντων τῶν Μάγων* / "And when the wise men had departed"). Paragraphs 37–38 govern the case where the Sunday after the Nativity (Holy Ancestors: David the King, Joseph the Betrothed, and James the Brother of the Lord) coincides with the Apodosis of the Feast on Sunday, December 31. On Saturday evening (§ 37), Great Vespers at "Lord, I have cried" features 10 Stichira (3 Resurrectional, 4 Festal Idiomela *Δεῦτε ἀγαλλιασώμεθα*, and 3 of the Ancestors of God); "Glory" (*Μνήμην ἐπιτελοῦμεν*); "Both now and ever" (*Αὐγούστου μοναρχήσαντος*); Entrance, *Φῶς ἱλαρόν*, Prokeimenon; Aposticha Resurrectional with "Glory" of the Ancestors (*Ἱερέων μνήμη*), "Both now and ever" (*Σπηλαίῳ παρῴκησας*); Dismissal Troparia: Resurrectional, of the Ancestors (*Εὐαγγελίζου, Ἰωσήφ*), and of the Feast (*Ἡ γέννησίς σου*). On Sunday Matins (§ 38), after Psalm 50 [LXX], the Triadic Canon and Triadic hymns (*Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*) are sung, followed by the Trisagion Prayers, Troparion *Ἡ γέννησίς σου*, and Hexapsalmos; "God is the Lord", Troparia as at Vespers; Psalter and Amomos (Kathisma 17 / Psalm 118 LXX); Resurrectional Kathismata with Festal Kathismata instead of Theotokia; Evlogitaria, Hypakoe, Anavathmoi of the Tone, Prokeimenon; Canons of the Resurrection, of the Feast (*Δόξα σοι ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν*), and of Joseph the Betrothed (*Χριστοῦ θεράπων μακάριε*); after Ode 3, Resurrectional Kontakion and Ikos plain, Kathisma *Πατρὸς ὡς ἀληθῶς*, "Both now and ever" *Χορὸς τῶν Προφητῶν*; after Ode 6, Kontakion and Ikos of the Sunday after the Nativity, Menologion and Synaxarion; double Katavasiai of the Nativity (*Ἔσωσε λαόν* and *Στείβει θαλάσσης*); Morning Gospel order; Ode 9 from both festal canons with their Megalynaria and both Katavasiai of Ode 9; Exapostilaria of the Resurrection, Ancestors, and Feast; Praises with 4 Resurrectional and 4 Festal Stichira; "Glory" (*Αἷμα καὶ πῦρ*), "Both now and ever" (*Ὑπερευλογημένη*), and Great Doxology.

[^212]: Divine Liturgy of the Sunday after the Nativity and Apodosis (§ 39); Situation Five: Nativity falling on Tuesday, Wednesday, or Thursday (§ 40); and Sunday after the Nativity during the Afterfeast (Saturday Vespers § 41 and Sunday Matins § 42). Physical leaf p305 (printed page 290) and facing English leaf p306 (printed page 291) conclude the Liturgy for Situation Four and open Situation Five (Ε΄). At the Divine Liturgy of the Sunday after the Nativity and Apodosis (§ 39), the Antiphons of the Feast are sung with the Second Antiphon refrain *Ὁ ἐκ Παρθένου τεχθείς* ("Who wast born of a Virgin"); Entrance Verse of the Feast with the Sunday addition *Ὁ ἀναστὰς ἐκ νεκρῶν* ("Who art risen from the dead"); Dismissal Troparia: Resurrectional, Festal (*Ἡ γέννησίς σου*), Ancestors (*Εὐαγγελίζου, Ἰωσήφ*), and Temple Patron; Kontakion *Ἡ Παρθένος σήμερον*; Trisagion Hymn; Epistle (2 Timothy 4:5–8) and Gospel (Mark 1:1–8) of the Sunday before Theophany; at "Especially", the Festal Megalynarion and Heirmos of Ode 9 *Μεγάλυνον ἡ ψυχή μου . . . Στέργειν μὲν ἡμᾶς*; Communion Verse Psalm 110:9 LXX (*Λύτρωσιν ἀπέστειλε* / "The Lord hath sent redemption unto His people"); Dismissal Troparion *Ἡ γέννησίς σου*, Dismissal. Situation Five (§ 40) governs Christmas occurring on Tuesday, Wednesday, or Thursday: the Paramony Royal Hours, Great Vespers, and Liturgy of Saint Basil the Great, as well as the festal services and the Synaxis of the Theotokos, follow Situation One §§ 1–11. Paragraphs 41–42 detail the celebration of the Sunday after the Nativity when it occurs on an intermediate day of the afterfeast (between Dec 26 and 31). On Saturday evening (§ 41), Great Vespers at "Lord, I have cried" has 10 Stichira (4 Resurrectional, 3 Festal Idiomela *Δεῦτε ἀγαλλιασώμεθα*, 3 of the Ancestors of God); "Glory" (*Μνήμην ἐπιτελοῦμεν*); "Both now and ever": First Theotokion Dogmatikon of the Tone (distinct from Situation Four, where the festal Doxastikon is sung); Entrance, *Φῶς ἱλαρόν*, Prokeimenon; Aposticha Resurrectional with "Glory" of the Ancestors (*Ἱερέων μνήμη*), "Both now and ever" (*Χορεύουσιν Ἄγγελοι*); Dismissal Troparia: Resurrectional, Ancestors (*Εὐαγγελίζου, Ἰωσήφ*), Festal (*Ἡ γέννησίς σου*), Dismissal. On Sunday Matins (§ 42), after Psalm 50 [LXX], Triadic Canon and Triadic hymns (*Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*), Trisagion Prayers, Troparion *Ἡ γέννησίς σου*, Hexapsalmos; "God is the Lord", Troparia as at Vespers; Psalter and Amomos; Resurrectional Kathismata with afterfeast Kathismata instead of Theotokia; Evlogitaria, Hypakoe, Anavathmoi of the Tone, Prokeimenon; Canons of the Resurrection and of Joseph the Betrothed (the festal canon being omitted here); after Ode 3, Resurrectional Kontakion and Ikos plain, Kathisma *Πατρὸς ὡς ἀληθῶς*...

[^213]: Situation Five Concluded: Matins and Divine Liturgy of the Sunday after the Nativity (§§ 42 concl., 43); Month of January: January 1, Circumcision of our Lord Jesus Christ and Commemoration of Saint Basil the Great (Vespers § 1 and opening of Matins § 2). Physical leaf p307 (printed page 292) and facing English leaf p308 (printed page 293) conclude the five Situations of the Nativity and begin the Month of January. Matins of the Sunday after the Nativity under Situation Five (§ 42 concl.) concludes with Kathisma "Both now and ever" *Χορὸς τῶν Προφητῶν*; after Ode 6: Kontakion of the Sunday after the Nativity (*Εὐφροσύνης σήμερον* / "Of joy today") and Ikos (*Ἀπορρήτῳ βουλῇ* / "By ineffable counsel"), Menologion and Synaxarion; Katavasiai *Ἔσωσε λαόν* (single canon only); Morning Gospel order; Magnificat (*Τὴν τιμιωτέραν* is sung); Exapostilaria of Resurrection, Ancestors, and Feast; Praises with 4 Resurrectional and 4 Festal Stichira (*Εὐφραίνεσθε, δίκαιοι*); "Glory" (*Αἷμα καὶ πῦρ*), "Both now and ever" (*Ὑπερευλογημένη*), Great Doxology, and *Σήμερον σωτηρία*. At the Divine Liturgy (§ 43): Typika and 4 Beatitudes of the Tone, and 4 from Ode 6 of Canon of the Betrothed; Entrance with Resurrectional Dismissal Troparion, *Ἡ γέννησίς σου*, *Εὐαγγελίζου, Ἰωσήφ*, Temple Patron, Kontakion *Ἡ Παρθένος σήμερον*; Epistle Galatians 1:11–19, Gospel Matthew 2:13–23; at "Especially": *Ἄξιόν ἐστιν* (normal Megalynarion, since it is an intermediate day and not the Apodosis); Communion Verse Psalm 148:1 LXX (*Αἰνεῖτε τὸν Κύριον* / "Praise the Lord from the heavens"); *Εἴδομεν τὸ φῶς*, Dismissal. Formal rubric closes: *End of the five Situations of the Feast of the Nativity of Christ.* The Month of January opens on January 1 with the Circumcision of Christ and Saint Basil the Great. At Vespers (§ 1): Introductory Psalm [Ps. 103 LXX], First Stasis of the First Kathisma [Ps. 1–3 LXX]; at "Lord, I have cried", 6 Stichira (2 Festal Idiomela repeating the first, 3 Prosomoia of Saint Basil); "Glory" of the Saint (*Σοφίας ἐραστής*); "Both now and ever" (*Συγκαταβαίνων ὁ Σωτήρ*); Entrance, *Φῶς ἱλαρόν*, Prokeimenon of the day, 3 Old Testament Readings (Genesis 17:1–14; Proverbs 8:22–30; Proverbs 10:31–11:12); Aposticha: 3 Idiomela of the Saint, "Glory" (*Ὁ τὴν χάριν τῶν θαυμάτων*), "Both now and ever" (*Οὐκ ἐπῃσχύνθη ὁ πανάγαθος Θεός*); Dismissal Troparion of the Saint (*Εἰς πᾶσαν τὴν γῆν*), then "Glory... Both now and ever...": of the Feast once (*Μορφὴν ἀναλλοιώτως*), and the festal Dismissal (*Ὁ ἐν τῇ ὀγδόῃ ἡμέρᾳ σαρκὶ περιτμηθῆναι καταδεξάμενος διὰ τὴν ἡμῶν σωτηρίαν Χριστὸς ὁ ἀληθινὸς Θεὸς ἡμῶν...*). At Matins (§ 2): after Psalm 50 [LXX], Lite of the Saint; Trisagion Prayers, Troparion *Μορφὴν ἀναλλοιώτως*, Hexapsalmos.

[^214]: January 1 Matins Concluded (§ 2) and Complete Festal Megalynaria of Ode 9 for the Circumcision of Christ and Saint Basil the Great. Physical leaf p309 (printed page 294) and facing English leaf p310 (printed page 295) conclude Matins for January 1. At "God is the Lord": Dismissal Troparion of Saint Basil twice, and of the Feast once; Psalter of the day and Polyeleos; Kathismata in order; Anavathmoi: First Antiphon of Tone 4 (*Ἐκ νεότητός μου*); Prokeimenon: Violakis notes *Εἰς πᾶσαν τὴν γῆν ἐξῆλθεν ὁ φθόγγος αὐτοῦ* [Ps. 18:5 LXX], adding the critical rubrical note that the Menaion and standard liturgical sources indicate *Τὸ στόμα μου λαλήσει σοφίαν* ("My mouth shall speak wisdom", Psalm 48:4 LXX); *Πᾶσα πνοή*; Morning Gospel (John 10:1–9, from November 13); Psalm 50 [LXX] plain; "Glory": *Ταῖς τοῦ Ἱεράρχου*; "Both now and ever": *Ταῖς τῆς Θεοτόκου*; Verse Psalm 50:3 LXX (*Ἐλέησόν με, ὁ Θεός*); Idiomelon *Ἐξεχύθη ἡ χάρις ἐν χείλεσί σου* (Tone 6); Canon of the Feast *Δεῦτε λαοί* with Verse *Δόξα σοι ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν*, and Canon of Saint Basil *Σοῦ τὴν φωνήν* with Verse *Ἅγιε τοῦ Θεοῦ*; after Ode 3, Kathismata of Saint Basil and the Feast; after Ode 6, Kontakion and Ikos of Saint Basil, and Menologion; double Katavasiai of Theophany (*Βυθοῦ ἀνεκάλυψε πυθμένα* and *Στείβει θαλάσσης*); Ode 9 of both Feast and Saint sung with their respective Megalynaria. The leaf provides the complete text of the Megalynaria for Ode 9: for Canon 1 (Circumcision), 5 refrains (including the Menaion addition in brackets: "Today the Master is circumcised in the flesh, fulfilling the Law as an infant"); and for Canon 2 (Saint Basil), 4 refrains (including the Menaion additions in brackets: "Magnify, O my soul, the most bright luminary of the universe" and "Magnify, O my soul, the adorner of the Church of Christ"). The footnote preserves Violakis's editorial asterisk indicating that these bracketed refrains are commonly chanted in contemporary practice.

On Sunday Matins (§ 5 opening): after Psalm 50 [LXX], Triadic Canon, Triadic hymns *Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*, Trisagion Prayers, Troparion *Ἀπεστρέφετό ποτε*, Hexapsalmos; "God is the Lord", Resurrectional Troparion twice, Forefeast once; Psalter and Amomos; Resurrectional Kathismata in order, Evlogitaria, Hypakoe of the Tone, Anavathmoi, Prokeimenon; Canons of the Resurrection and Forefeast (*Χριστὸς μολεῖ πρὸς τὸ βάπτισμα* / "Christ cometh unto baptism") with Verse "Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee"; after Ode 3, Resurrectional Kontakion and Ikos...

[^219]: Sunday before Theophany: Situation Two Concluded (Matins § 5 concl., Divine Liturgy § 6), Great Blessing of the Waters on Paramony; and Feast of Holy Theophany (January 6): Situation One: Feast falling on Friday (Royal Hours on Thursday, Vespers and Liturgy of Saint Basil § 1). Physical leaf p319 (printed page 304) and facing English leaf p320 (printed page 305) conclude the Sunday before Theophany and commence the Feast of the Holy Theophany of our Lord and God and Savior Jesus Christ. Sunday Matins of Situation Two concludes (§ 5 concl.): after Ode 3, Kathisma *Ὁ μέγας ὑετός* ("The great rain" from January 5); after Ode 6, Kontakion of the Forefeast *Ἐν τοῖς ῥείθροις σήμερον*, Ikos, Menologion of the day; Katavasiai *Βυθοῦ ἀνεκάλυψε πυθμένα*; Morning Gospel order; Magnificat (*Τὴν τιμιωτέραν*); Exapostilaria: Resurrectional and Forefeast *Πῶς ῥεῖθρά σε ποτάμια*; Praises: 4 Resurrectional and 4 Forefeast Stichira (*Ἰδοὺ ὁ Βασιλεύς* / "Behold the King"); "Glory": Forefeast Doxastikon *Ἰωάννη Βαπτιστά*; "Both now and ever": *Ὑπερευλογημένη*; Great Doxology, and *Σήμερον σωτηρία*. At the Divine Liturgy (§ 6): Typika and Beatitudes (4 of Tone, 4 from Ode 6 of Forefeast Canon); Entrance with Resurrectional Troparion, Forefeast Troparion *Ἀπεστρέφετό ποτε*, Temple Patron, Kontakion *Ἐν τοῖς ῥείθροις σήμερον*; Epistle (2 Timothy 4:5–8) and Gospel (Mark 1:1–8) of the Sunday before Theophany; at "Especially": *Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*; Communion Verse Psalm 148:1 LXX; *Εἴδομεν τὸ φῶς*. Immediately following the Prayer Behind the Ambon and *Εἴη τὸ ὄνομα Κυρίου* ("Blessed be the name of the Lord"), the clergy proceed to the solemn Great Blessing of the Waters (Μέγας Ἁγιασμός): the choir chants the Idiomela *Φωνὴ Κυρίου ἐπὶ τῶν ὑδάτων* ("The voice of the Lord is upon the waters"), and the office is performed according to the Menaion; Dismissal Troparion of Theophany *Ἐν Ἰορδάνῃ βαπτιζομένου σου, Κύριε* ("When Thou, O Lord, wast baptized in the Jordan") and Kontakion *Ἐν τοῖς ῥείθροις σήμερον*; during the blessing and sprinkling of the faithful with holy water, the Second Choir chants the Idiomelon *᾿Ανυμνήσωμεν οἱ πιστοί* ("Let us, the faithful, praise"), followed by the Dismissal. At the trapeza, wine and olive oil are permitted in honor of the Sunday, relaxing the strict fast otherwise observed on the Eve of Theophany. The Feast of Holy Theophany (January 6) opens with Situation One (when January 6 falls on a Friday, § 1): on Thursday morning (January 5), following prescribed Matins, the Royal Hours alone are sung according to the order of the Eve of the Nativity (referencing Christmas Situation One § 2). Great Vespers joined to the Divine Liturgy of Saint Basil the Great with the Great Blessing of the Waters at the conclusion of the Liturgy are celebrated on Thursday afternoon according to the prescribed order.


## Cohort 33 Footnotes

[^220]: Eve of Holy Theophany (January 5) Concluded: Great Vespers Joined to the Divine Liturgy of Saint Basil the Great, Old Testament Readings, and Great Blessing of the Waters (§ 2); and Feast of Holy Theophany (January 6): Friday Matins Opening (§ 3). Physical leaf p321 (printed page 306) and facing English leaf p322 (printed page 307) govern the festive eve and opening of Holy Theophany when January 6 falls on a Friday. Great Vespers joined to the Divine Liturgy of Saint Basil the Great (§ 2) begins following the Dismissal of the Ninth Hour: the Deacon intones the opening blessing (*Εὐλόγησον, Δέσποτα* / "Bless, Master"), the Priest gives the doxological exclamation *Εὐλογημένη ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ Πατρός* ("Blessed is the kingdom of the Father..."), and the Patriarch (or presiding Hierarch) reads the Introductory Psalm [Ps. 103 LXX], followed by the Great Litany. At "Lord, I have cried" (*Κύριε ἐκέκραξα*), 6 Stichira are chanted: the 4 Idiomela of the Feast (*Τὸν φωτισμὸν ἡμῶν* / "Our illumination") repeating the first two; "Glory... Both now and ever...": *Ὑπέκλινας κάραν τῷ Προδρόμῳ* ("Thou hast bowed Thy head unto the Forerunner"). The Little Entrance is made with the Holy Gospel Book, followed by *Φῶς ἱλαρόν* ("O Gladsome Light") and the thirteen Old Testament Readings of the Eve. Following Reading 3 (Genesis 1:1–13: *Ἐν ἀρχῇ ἐποίησεν ὁ Θεός* / "In the beginning God created"), the First Choir intones the Troparion *Ἐπεφάνης ἐν τῷ κόσμῳ* ("Thou hast appeared in the world"), and the Second Choir responds with the choral refrain *Ἵνα φωτίσῃς τοὺς ἐν σκότει καθημένους, Φιλάνθρωπε, δόξα σοι* ("To give light to those who sit in darkness; O Lover of mankind, glory to Thee!"), sung alternately between the verses of Psalm 66 LXX until the Canonarch concludes. Following Reading 6 (4 Kingdoms 2:6–14 LXX / 2 Kings 2:6–14: *Εἶπεν Ἠλίας τῷ Ἐλισσαιέ* / "And Elijah said unto Elisha"), the Second Choir intones the Troparion *Ἁμαρτωλοῖς καὶ τελώναις* ("Unto sinners and tax-collectors"), and the choral refrain *Ποῦ γὰρ εἶχε τὸ φῶς σου λάμψαι* ("Where indeed should Thy light have shone...") is alternated between the verses of Psalm 92 LXX. Following Reading 13 (4 Kingdoms 5:1–14 LXX / 2 Kings 5:1–14: *Παραγένετο Νεεμὰν βασιλέως Ἀσσυρίων* / "So Naaman, captain of the host of the king of Syria [printed Ἀσσυρίων]"), the Small Litany is intoned, the Trisagion Hymn is chanted, followed by the Epistle (1 Corinthians 9:19–27), "Alleluia", and the Holy Gospel (Luke 3:1–18) proclaimed from the ambo, followed by the Divine Liturgy of Saint Basil the Great. The Communion Verse is Psalm 148:1 LXX (*Αἰνεῖτε τὸν Κύριον* / "Praise the Lord from the heavens"), followed by *Εἴδομεν τὸ φῶς τὸ ἀληθινόν* ("We have seen the true light"). After the Prayer behind the Ambon, the clergy proceed to the solea for the solemn Great Blessing of the Waters (*Μέγας Ἁγιασμός*): the choirs chant the Idiomela *Φωνὴ Κυρίου ἐπὶ τῶν ὑδάτων* ("The voice of the Lord is upon the waters"), and the office is celebrated according to the Menaion; during the sprinkling of the faithful, the Second Choir sings the Idiomelon *Ἀνυμνήσωμεν οἱ πιστοί* ("Let us, the faithful, praise"), followed by the solemn festal Dismissal with its proper characteristic incipit: *Ὁ ἐν Ἰορδάνῃ ὑπὸ Ἰωάννου βαπτισθῆναι καταδεξάμενος διὰ τὴν ἡμῶν σωτηρίαν, Χριστὸς ὁ ἀληθινὸς Θεὸς ἡμῶν* ("May He Who deigned to be baptized by John in the Jordan for our salvation, Christ our true God..."). The rubrics prescribe xerophagy (*ξηροφαγία*, strict fast without wine or oil) at table on this eve. Paragraph 3 opens Friday Matins for the feast: following Psalm 50 [LXX], the Lite and the Idiomela of the Aposticha (omitted on the eve due to the vigil Liturgy) are chanted; then the Trisagion Prayers, the Dismissal Troparion of Theophany *Ἐν Ἰορδάνῃ βαπτιζομένου σου, Κύριε* ("When Thou, O Lord, wast baptized in the Jordan"), and the Hexapsalmos; at "God is the Lord", the Dismissal Troparion is chanted thrice, followed by the Psalter Kathismata and the festal Polyeleos (*Αἰνεῖτε τὸ ὄνομα Κυρίου*, Psalm 134 LXX; the printed English column incorrectly labels this Psalm 135 LXX by confusing Masoretic numbering).

[^221]: Feast of Holy Theophany (January 6) Continued: Friday Matins Gospel Order, Canons, and Festive Megalynaria of the Ninth Ode (§ 3 cont.). Physical leaf p323 (printed page 308) and facing English leaf p324 (printed page 309) provide the rubrical sequence of Friday Matins from the Kathismata through the Ninth Ode. Following the 3 Kathisma sedalia, the Anavathmoi of Tone 4 (First Antiphon *Ἐκ νεότητός μου* / "From my youth") are sung, followed by the Prokeimenon from Psalm 113:3 LXX (*Ἡ θάλασσα εἶδε καὶ ἔφυγεν, ὁ Ἰορδάνης ἐστράφη εἰς τὰ ὀπίσω* / "The sea saw and fled, Jordan was driven back"). After *Πᾶσα πνοὴ αἰνεσάτω τὸν Κύριον* ("Let everything that hath breath praise the Lord"), the Matins Gospel is proclaimed (Mark 1:9–11), followed by Psalm 50 [LXX] read simply; "Glory": *Τὰ σύμπαντα σήμερον ἀγαλλιάσθω* ("Today let all things greatly rejoice"); "Both now and ever": the same; Verse: *Ἐλέησόν με, ὁ Θεός* (Ps. 50:3 LXX) and the Idiomelon *Θεὸς λόγος ἐπεφάνη ἐν σαρκί* ("God the Word appeared in the flesh"). Both Canons of the Feast are chanted with 4 troparia each, without verses except for "Glory... Both now and ever..." in each Ode: the First Canon by Saint Cosmas the Melodist in Tone 2 (*Βυθοῦ ἀνεκάλυψε πυθμένα* / "He uncovered the bottom of the deep") and the Second Iambic Canon by Saint John Damascene in Tone 2 (*Στείβει θαλάσσης* / "The Lord, working wonders"). After Ode 3, the Hypakoe *Ὅτε τῇ ἐπιφανείᾳ σου* ("When at Thy manifestation"); after Ode 6, the Kontakion *Ἐπεφάνης σήμερον τῇ οἰκουμένῃ* ("Thou hast appeared today to the universe"), the Ikos, and the Menologion. Both Katavasiai are sung in full at each Ode. At Ode 9, the Magnificat (*Τὴν τιμιωτέραν*) is not sung; instead, the festive Megalynaria (*Μεγαλυνάρια*) are appointed for each troparion. For the First Canon, four primary Megalynaria are given: (1) *Μεγάλυνον ψυχή μου, τὴν τιμιωτέραν τῶν ἄνω στρατευμάτων* ("Magnify, O my soul, Her that is more honorable than the heavenly hosts"); (2) *Μεγάλυνον ψυχή μου, τὸν ἐν Ἰορδάνῃ ἐλθόντα βαπτισθῆναι* ("Magnify, O my soul, Him Who hath come to be baptized in the Jordan"); (3) *Μεγάλυνον ψυχή μου, τὸν ὑπὸ Προδρόμου τὸ βάπτισμα αἰτοῦντα [λαβόντα]* ("Magnify, O my soul, Him Who asketh [receiveth] baptism from the Forerunner"); (4) *Μεγάλυνον ψυχή μου, τὸν ἐκ τῆς Πατρῴας φωνῆς μαρτυρηθέντα* ("Magnify, O my soul, Him to Whom the voice of the Father bore witness"). Three additional bracketed Megalynaria marked with asterisks are preserved from the modern printed Athenian Menaion tradition (ed. Phos, 1960; Apostoliki Diakonia, 1991), although absent from the classical textus receptus of the Violakis Typikon: (5) *Μεγάλυνον ψυχή μου, τὸν ἕνα τῆς Τριάδος, κλίναντα τὸν αὐχένα, καὶ βάπτισμα λαβόντα* ("Magnify, O my soul, One of the Trinity Who bowed His head and received baptism"); (6) *Προφῆτα, δεῦρο πρός με, ἔκτεινον τὴν χεῖρα, καὶ βάπτισόν με τάχος* ("O Prophet, come unto Me: stretch out thy hand and baptize Me swiftly"); (7) *Προφῆτα, ἄφες ἄρτι, καὶ βάπτισόν με θέλων· πληρῶσαι καὶ γὰρ ἦλθον, πᾶσαν δικαιοσύνην* ("O Prophet, suffer it to be so now, and baptize Me willing: for I have come to fulfill all righteousness"). For the Second Iambic Canon, five Megalynaria are provided: (1) *Σήμερον ὁ Δεσπότης, κλίνει τὸν αὐχένα, χειρὶ τῇ τοῦ Προδρόμου* ("Today the Master bows His head beneath the hand of the Forerunner"); (2) *Σήμερον Ἰωάννης, βαπτίζει τὸν Δεσπότην, ἐν ῥείθροις Ἰορδάνου* ("Today John baptizes the Master in the streams of the Jordan"); and three bracketed Menaion additions: (3) *Σήμερον ὁ Δεσπότης, νάμασιν ἐνθάπτει, βροτῶν τὴν ἁμαρτίαν* ("Today the Master buries in the waters the sin of mortal man"); (4) *Σήμερον ὁ Δεσπότης, ἄνωθεν μαρτυρεῖται, Υἱὸς ἠγαπημένος* ("Today the Master receives testimony from on high, that He is the beloved Son"); (5) *Σήμερον ὁ Δεσπότης, ἦλθεν ἁγιάσαι, τὴν φύσιν τῶν ὑδάτων* ("Today the Master has come to sanctify the nature of the waters").

[^222]: Feast of Holy Theophany (January 6) Continued: Conclusion of Matins Ode 9, Praises, Great Doxology, and Great Blessing of the Waters Rite (§ 3 concl.). Physical leaf p325 (printed page 310) and facing English leaf p326 (printed page 311) conclude the Ninth Ode and detail the Great Blessing of the Waters celebrated at the climax of the Great Doxology. Ode 9 concludes with the final Megalynaria: *Σήμερον ὁ Δεσπότης, τὸ βάπτισμα λαμβάνει, ὑπὸ χειρὸς Προδρόμου* ("Today the Master receives baptism at the hand of the Forerunner"); "Glory": *Μεγάλυνον ψυχή μου, τῆς τρισυποστάτου, καὶ ἀδιαιρέτου, θεότητος τὸ κράτος* ("Magnify, O my soul, the power of the Godhead in three Persons and undivided"); "Both now and ever": *Μεγάλυνον ψυχή μου, τὴν λυτρωσαμένην, ἡμᾶς ἐκ τῆς κατάρας* ("Magnify, O my soul, Her who hath delivered us from the curse"). Matins continues with the Exapostilarion chanted thrice; at the Praises: 6 Idiomela (*Φῶς ἐκ φωτός* / "Light from Light"); "Glory": *Νάματα Ἰορδάνεια* ("O Savior, Who clothedst Thyself with the waters of Jordan"); "Both now and ever": *Σήμερον ὁ Χριστός* ("Today Christ"), and the Great Doxology. In the Great Doxology, an ancient Constantinopolitan rubrical custom replaces the customary opening verse *Δόξα σοι τῷ δείξαντι τὸ φῶς* ("Glory to Thee Who hast shown us the light") with the concluding refrain of the Theotokion: "We who have been enlightened cry aloud: Glory to God made manifest, Who hath appeared upon earth and brought light unto the world." Immediately following the third repetition of the Trisagion (*Ἅγιος ἀθάνατος, ἐλέησον ἡμᾶς*) at the end of the Doxology, the clergy and choirs transition directly into the solemn Great Blessing of the Waters: the choirs chant the 3 Idiomela of Saint Sophronius of Jerusalem (*Φωνὴ Κυρίου ἐπὶ τῶν ὑδάτων* / "The voice of the Lord is upon the waters"), "Glory... Both now and ever...": *Πρὸς τὴν φωνὴν τοῦ βοῶντος ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ* ("At the voice of one crying in the wilderness"). The Priest exits through the Holy Doors carrying the Precious Cross on his head, preceded by candle-bearers and Deacons; the Patriarch (or presiding Hierarch), vested in epitrachilion and small omophorion, descends from his Throne to the center of the temple where the water vessel has been prepared. The Canonarch reads the three Prophecies (Isaiah 35:1–10; 55:1–13; 12:3–6), followed by the Epistle (1 Corinthians 10:1–4) and the Gospel (Mark 1:9–11) proclaimed by the Patriarch. Following the polychronion (*Εἰς πολλὰ ἔτη*), the Great Archdeacon intones the Great Litany of the Blessing while the Patriarch recites silently the secret prayer *Κύριε Ἰησοῦ Χριστέ* ("O Lord Jesus Christ"), culminating in the aloud exclamation *Τριὰς ὑπερούσιε* ("O Trinity transcending essence") and the great festive prayer *Μέγας εἶ, Κύριε, καὶ θαυμαστὰ τὰ ἔργα σου* ("Great art Thou, O Lord, and marvelous are Thy works"), repeated thrice with the choral acclamation *Δόξα σοι, Κύριε, δόξα σοι!* ("Glory to Thee, O Lord, glory to Thee!"). A critical apparatus note in both Greek and English facsimile columns addresses a numbering error in the 1888 edition, where Violakis misnumbered this footnote as footnote 4 instead of 1; the note documents the pastoral practice emerging in parish churches of delaying the Great Blessing of the Waters until after the Divine Liturgy to prevent disorder and accommodate late-arriving faithful.

[^223]: Feast of Holy Theophany (January 6) Continued: Conclusion of the Great Blessing of the Waters and Divine Liturgy Antiphons 1 & 2 (§ 4 opening). Physical leaf p327 (printed page 312) and facing English leaf p328 (printed page 313) conclude the solemn sanctification of waters and commence the festal Divine Liturgy of Saint John Chrysostom. Following the thrice-repeated prayer *Μέγας εἶ, Κύριε*, the celebrant immerses the Precious Cross into the water vessel three times with the sprinkler (*ἁγιαστήρ*), chanting each time the Dismissal Troparion of Theophany: *Ἐν Ἰορδάνῃ βαπτιζομένου σου, Κύριε* ("When Thou, O Lord, wast baptized in the Jordan"), repeated by each choir. He then sprinkles the congregation cruciformly with the newly consecrated water while chanting the Kontakion *Ἐπεφάνης σήμερον τῇ οἰκουμένῃ* ("Thou hast appeared today to the universe"). As the Patriarch ascends the Throne amidst choral acclamations (*Εἰς πολλὰ ἔτη*), he sprinkles the concelebrating Hierarchs and clergy; during this sprinkling, the choirs chant slowly and melodiously the Troparion from Ode 8 of the Canon: *Τριάδος ἡ φανέρωσις* ("The manifestation of the Trinity"). The Second Choir then chants the Dismissal Troparion *Ἐν Ἰορδάνῃ*, and the Divine Liturgy of Saint John Chrysostom commences immediately. At the Divine Liturgy (§ 4), the special festive Antiphons of Theophany are chanted in Tone 2: First Antiphon verses from Psalm 113:1, 2, 3, 5 LXX (*Ἐν ἐξόδῳ Ἰσραὴλ ἐξ Αἰγύπτου, οἴκου Ἰακώβ* / "When Israel went out of Egypt, the house of Jacob from a barbarian people"; *Ἐγενήθη Ἰουδαία ἁγίασμα αὐτοῦ, Ἰσραὴλ ἐξουσία αὐτοῦ* / "Judea became His sanctuary, and Israel His dominion"; *Ἡ θάλασσα εἶδε καὶ ἔφυγεν· ὁ Ἰορδάνης ἐστράφη εἰς τὰ ὀπίσω* / "The sea saw and fled; the Jordan turned back"; *Τί σοί ἐστι θάλασσα, ὅτι ἔφυγες; καὶ σὺ Ἰορδάνη, ὅτι ἐστράφης εἰς τὰ ὀπίσω;* / "What ailed thee, O sea, that thou didst flee? And thou, Jordan, that thou didst turn back?"); refrain: *Ταῖς πρεσβείαις τῆς Θεοτόκου, Σῶτερ, σῶσον ἡμᾶς* ("Through the intercessions of the Theotokos, Savior, save us"). Second Antiphon verses from Psalm 114:1, 2, 3, 5 LXX (*Ἠγάπησα, ὅτι εἰσακούσεται Κύριος τῆς φωνῆς τῆς δεήσεώς μου* / "I am well pleased that the Lord will hear the voice of my prayer"; *Ὅτι ἔκλινε τὸ οὖς αὐτοῦ ἐμοί, καὶ ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις μου ἐπικαλέσομαι* / "For He hath inclined His ear unto me, and in my days will I call upon Him"; *Περιέσχον με ὠδῖνες θανάτου, κίνδυνοι ᾅδου εὕροσάν με* / "The pangs of death compassed me, the perils of Hades found me; I found tribulation and sorrow"; *Ἐλεήμων ὁ Κύριος καὶ δίκαιος, καὶ ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν ἐλεεῖ* / "Merciful is the Lord, and righteous; yea, our God is merciful").

[^224]: Feast of Holy Theophany (January 6) Concluded: Divine Liturgy Antiphon 3, Little Entrance, Epistle, Gospel, and Dismissal (§ 4 concl.); and Synaxis of the Honorable and Glorious Prophet, Forerunner, and Baptist John (January 7): Friday Vespers (§ 5). Physical leaf p329 (printed page 314) and facing English leaf p330 (printed page 315) conclude the festal Divine Liturgy of Theophany and commence the post-festal Synaxis of the Forerunner celebrated on the following day. At the Divine Liturgy (§ 4 concl.), the Second Antiphon concludes with the refrain *Σῶσον ἡμᾶς Υἱὲ Θεοῦ, ὁ ἐν Ἰορδάνῃ ὑπὸ Ἰωάννου βαπτισθείς, ψάλλοντάς σοι, Ἀλληλούϊα* ("Save us, O Son of God, Who wast baptized by John in the Jordan, who sing to Thee: Alleluia"), followed by *Ὁ Μονογενὴς Υἱὸς καὶ Λόγος τοῦ Θεοῦ* ("Only-begotten Son and Immortal Word of God"). The Third Antiphon is chanted in Tone 1 to verses from Psalm 117:1–4 LXX (*Ἐξομολογεῖσθε τῷ Κυρίῳ, ὅτι ἀγαθός, ὅτι εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα τὸ ἔλεος αὐτοῦ* / "O give thanks unto the Lord, for He is good, for His mercy endureth forever"; *Εἰπάτω δὴ οἶκος Ἰσραήλ...* / "Let the house of Israel now say..."; *Εἰπάτω δὴ οἶκος Ἀαρών...* / "Let the house of Aaron now say..."; *Εἰπάτωσαν δὴ πάντες οἱ φοβούμενοι τὸν Κύριον...* / "Let all that fear the Lord now say..."); refrain: Dismissal Troparion of Theophany *Ἐν Ἰορδάνῃ*. At the Little Entrance, the festive Introit Verse is chanted from Psalm 117:26, 27 LXX: *Εὐλογημένος ὁ ἐρχόμενος ἐν ὀνόματι Κυρίου, Θεὸς Κύριος καὶ ἐπέφανεν ἡμῖν. Σῶσον ἡμᾶς Υἱὲ Θεοῦ, ὁ ἐν Ἰορδάνῃ ὑπὸ Ἰωάννου βαπτισθείς, ψάλλοντάς σοι, Ἀλληλούϊα* ("Blessed is He that cometh in the name of the Lord; the Lord is God, and hath appeared unto us. Save us, O Son of God, Who wast baptized by John in the Jordan, who sing to Thee: Alleluia"). Troparia: Dismissal Troparion *Ἐν Ἰορδάνῃ*, and Kontakion *Ἐπεφάνης σήμερον*. Instead of the Trisagion Hymn, the baptismal hymn is chanted: *Ὅσοι εἰς Χριστὸν ἐβαπτίσθητε, Χριστὸν ἐνεδύσασθε. Ἀλληλούϊα* ("All of you who have been baptized into Christ have put on Christ. Alleluia", Galatians 3:27). The Epistle of the Feast is Titus 2:11–14; 3:4–7; the Gospel is Matthew 3:13–17. At "Especially", instead of the Axion Estin, the Heirmos of Ode 9 is chanted: *Μεγάλυνον ψυχή μου τὴν τιμιωτέραν καὶ ἐνδοξοτέραν τῶν ἄνω στρατευμάτων. Ἀπορεῖ πᾶσα γλῶσσα* ("Magnify, O my soul, Her that is more honorable and more glorious than the heavenly hosts. Every tongue is at a loss to praise Thee worthily..."). The Communion Verse is Titus 2:11: *Ἐπεφάνη ἡ χάρις τοῦ Θεοῦ ἡ σωτήριος πᾶσιν ἀνθρώποις* ("The grace of God that bringeth salvation hath appeared unto all men"); instead of *Εἴδομεν τὸ φῶς*, Dismissal Troparion *Ἐν Ἰορδάνῃ*, and the Dismissal. On Friday evening (§ 5), the Synaxis of the Honorable and Glorious Prophet, Forerunner, and Baptist John (*Ἡ Σύναξις τοῦ τιμίου Προδρόμου*) is celebrated at Great Vespers: after the Introductory Psalm [Ps. 103 LXX], at "Lord, I have cried" (*Κύριε ἐκέκραξα*), 6 Stichira are chanted: 3 Idiomela of the Feast (*Τὸν φωτισμὸν ἡμῶν*) and 3 Prosomoia of the Forerunner (*Πανεύφημε Πρόδρομε Χριστοῦ*); "Glory": *Ἔνσαρκε λύχνε* ("O torch incarnate"); "Both now and ever": *Θεὸς λόγος ἐπεφάνη ἐν σαρκί* ("God the Word appeared in the flesh"). Entrance with *Φῶς ἱλαρόν*, followed by the Great Prokeimenon in Tone 7 from Psalm 113:11 LXX: *Ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ καὶ ἐν τῇ γῇ, πάντα ὅσα ἠθέλησεν ἐποίησεν* ("Our God is in heaven and on earth; all things whatsoever He hath willed, He hath done") with its four verses. At the Aposticha: 3 Prosomoia Stichira beginning *Ὡς εἶδέ σε Δέσποτα* ("When he saw Thee, O Master"); "Glory": *Ὡς τοῦ Πνεύματος ἐραστής* ("As a lover of the Spirit"); "Both now and ever": *Δεῦτε μιμησώμεθα* ("Come, let us imitate the wise virgins"); Dismissal Troparia: Theophany (*Ἐν Ἰορδάνῃ*), and Forerunner (*Μνήμη δικαίου μετ’ ἐγκωμίων* / "The memory of the righteous is celebrated with hymns of praise").

At § 31: on Saturday Matins, after Midnight Service, at "God is the Lord" (*Θεὸς Κύριος*), Dismissal Troparion *Ἑτοιμάζου Ζαβουλών* twice; Canons: Forefeast *Ὡς ἐν ἠπείρῳ πεζεύσας* ("Traversing the deep on foot as on dry land") and Seventy Apostles *Χριστῷ μαθητεύσαντες* ("Having been discipled unto Christ", from January 4); after Ode 6, Kontakion and Ikos of Forefeast, and Menologion; Heirmos of Ode 8, Magnificat *Τὴν τιμιωτέραν*. Exapostilaria: Seventy Apostles *Καταλιπόντες κόσμον* ("Having forsaken the world") and Forefeast *Ὁ ἐκ Πατρὸς ἀχρόνως* ("Begotten timelessly of the Father"); Praises *Σοὶ δόξα πρέπει*, and Aposticha. Divine Liturgy: Epistle (1 Timothy 3:14–4:5) and Gospel (Matthew 3:1–11) of the Saturday before the Lights; Communion Verse Psalm 64:5 LXX (*Μακάριοι οὓς ἐξελέξω καὶ προσελάβου, Κύριε* / "Blessed are they whom Thou hast chosen and taken unto Thyself, O Lord"); *Εἴδομεν τὸ φῶς*, and Dismissal. At § 32: on Saturday evening and Sunday morning, the office of Sunday before the Lights, Liturgy of Saint John Chrysostom, and Blessing of the Waters are celebrated as in Situation 2, § 4–6; dispensation for wine and oil at table. At § 33, Sunday evening Great Vespers opens with the Old Testament Readings, Troparia and verses...

Textual and Hymnographical Note: The Heirmos of the Eighth Ode of the First Canon to Saint Euthymius, composed by Saint John of Damascus, appears in later printed editions as *Παῖδας εὐαγεῖς ἐν τῇ καμίνῳ* ("The holy Children in the furnace"); however, the alphabetical acrostic *Ὄλβος πέφηνας γηγενῶν Εὐθύμιε* ("A wealth to mortals hast thou appeared, O Euthymius") demands that the Eighth Ode begin with the letter *Y* (Upsilon). Scholarly Rubrical Decree of Patriarch Constantine I the Byzantine concerning the Praises on Sundays: Explains the standard rubrical canon prescribing the Resurrectional Eothinon Doxastikon at "Glory..." at the Praises on ordinary Sundays of the year, but establishes that for the great Ecumenical Doctors Gregory the Theologian and John Chrysostom, out of just debt to their pastoral guidance and immortal writings illuminating the Catholic Church, when their commemorations coincide with a Sunday outside the Triodion, the Doxastikon of the Saint is chanted instead of the Eothinon, especially in the Great Church of Constantinople. Note on Footnote 3: When this commemoration occurs on a Sunday within the Triodion period, the Doxastikon of the Triodion is chanted at "Glory..." at the Praises. Ancient Patriarchal Ceremonial Rubric: In the Patriarchal Church of Constantinople, on the two feasts of Saint John Chrysostom (January 27 and November 13), when the Patriarch enters the church, he does not stand upon the central Patriarchal Throne, but in the Parathronion (side throne); upon the central Throne is enthroned the holy Icon of Chrysostom for veneration by the faithful; before the holy Icon stands the Patriarchal Dibamboulon (the great double-wick candelabrum), burning throughout the Divine Liturgy. § 4: Concurrence when Saint John Chrysostom falls on Sunday outside the Triodion: follows Saint Gregory (§§ 2, 3, 4). § 5: Concurrence when Saint John Chrysostom falls on Sunday within the Triodion: Saturday Great Vespers (4 Resurrectional Stichira, 2 of Triodion, 4 of Saint [on Meatfare Sunday: 3 of Triodion, 3 of Saint]; "Glory...": of Triodion; "Both now and ever...": first Theotokion of Tone; Little Entrance, Prokeimenon, Readings of Saint; Aposticha: Resurrectional Stichira, "Glory...": of Saint, "Both now and ever...": of Triodion; Dismissal Troparia: Resurrectional, Saint, Theotokion, Dismissal). § 6: Sunday Matins and Divine Liturgy within the Triodion: celebrated without alteration according to Saint Gregory (§§ 6, 7). § 7: Concurrence on the Saturday of Souls (Meatfare Saturday): office anticipated on Friday; Saturday of Souls celebrated on Saturday without transfer per Saint Gregory § 8. Following the initial Megalynarion *Ἀκατάληπτόν ἐστι* (inaugurated on leaf p380), the ninth ode of the Canon of the Meeting (composed by Saint Cosmas of Maiuma and embellished by the Byzantine sticheraric tradition) presents an alphabetical series of ten nine-syllable/twelve-syllable Megalynaria addressed alternately to the Theotokos, Christ, and the Righteous Symeon: (1) concluding verse of initial incipit: *Ἀγγέλοις καὶ βροτοῖς, Μητροπάρθενε ἁγνή* ["...unto angels and mortal men, O pure Virgin Mother"]; (2) *Ἀγκαλίζεται χερσίν, ὁ Πρεσβύτης Συμεών* ["Symeon the Elder takes in his arms the Maker of the Law and Master of all"]; (3) *Βουληθεὶς ὁ Πλαστουργός, ἵνα σώσῃ τὸν Ἀδάμ* ["The Creator, wishing to save Adam, took up His dwelling in thy pure and virgin womb"]; (4) *Γένος ἅπαν τῶν βροτῶν, μακαρίζει σε Ἁγνή* ["All the race of mortals blesseth thee, O Pure Virgin, and in faith glorifieth thee as Mother of God"]; (5) *Δεῦτε ἴδετε Χριστόν, τὸν Δεσπότην τοῦ παντός* ["Come and behold Christ, the Master of all, Whom Symeon beareth today in the temple"]; (6) *Ἐπιβλέπεις πρὸς τὴν γῆν, καὶ ποιεῖς τρέμειν αὐτήν* ["Thou lookest upon the earth and makest it tremble; how then can I, aged and weary, hold Thee in mine arms?"]; (7) *Ζήσας ἔτη Συμεών, ἕως εἶδε τὸν Χριστόν* ["Symeon lived for many years until he beheld Christ, and cried aloud unto Him: 'Now do I seek release'"]; (8) *Ἡ λαβὶς ἡ μυστική, ἡ τὸν ἄνθρακα Χριστόν* ["Thou art the mystic tongs, Mary, who hast conceived in thy womb Christ the live Coal" — drawing upon Isaiah 6:6]; (9) *Θέλων ἐνηνθρώπησας, ὁ προάναρχος Θεός* ["Of Thine own will Thou didst become man, O God without beginning, and art brought into the temple, forty days of age"]; (10) *Κατελθόντ’ ἐξ οὐρανοῦ, τὸν Δεσπότην τοῦ παντός* ["Symeon the priest received the Master of all, Who came down from heaven"]. Rubrical expansion of the 4 Troparia of Ode 9 to 6 with their proper appointed Megalynaria: Troparion 1 *Ἐν νόμῳ σκιᾷ* with Megalynarion *Λάμπρυνόν μου τὴν ψυχήν*; Troparion 2 with Megalynarion *Μητροπάρθενε ἁγνή, τί προσφέρεις*; Troparion 3 *Τοῖς πρὶν νεογνῶν* with Megalynarion *Νῦν ἀπόλυσιν ζητῶ*; Troparion 4 with Megalynarion *Ὃν οἱ ἄνω λειτουργοί*; Doxastikon (*Δόξα*) with Triadikon *Ἡ τῇ φύσει μὲν μονάς* ["O Thou Who art by nature One, but in Persons Three..."] paired with Megalynarion *Ἀπέδωκάς μοι*; and Theotokion (*Καὶ νῦν*) *Θεοτόκε ἡ ἐλπίς* ["O Theotokos, Hope of all Christians, shelter, guard, and preserve those whose hope is in thee..."] paired with Megalynarion *Ἱεροπρεπῶς ἀνθωμολογεῖτο*.

[^251]: Feast of the Meeting of our Lord Jesus Christ (Hypapante, February 2) — Matins Conclusion and Divine Liturgy (§ 3 incipit): Detailed epigraphic synthesis of physical leaf p383 (printed page 368) and facing English leaf p384 (printed page 369). Ἐν νόμῳ, σκιᾷ*; the Exapostilarion *Ἐν πνεύματι τῷ Ἱερῷ* ["The Elder, brought to the temple by the Spirit"] chanted thrice; at the Praises: the Stichira Prosomia *Νόμον τὸν ἐν γράμματι* ["Fulfilling the written Law"]; "Glory... Scholarly Note 1: Editorial note regarding the calendrical impossibility of the Apodosis of the Meeting occurring on a Sunday outside the Triodion period (under the Julian/Paschal calendar, Pascha falls between March 22 and April 25; the Triodion begins between January 11 and February 15; if February 9 falls on a Sunday, it is invariably within the Triodion, either as Sunday of the Publican and the Pharisee, Prodigal Son, or Meatfare). § 11 incipit: Situation II: Concurrence when February 2 falls on a Sunday within the Triodion period: Saturday Great Vespers (at "Lord, I have cried": 4 Resurrectional Stichira, 2 of Triodion, and 4 of Feast [on Meatfare and Cheesefare Sundays: 4 Resurrectional, 3 of Triodion, 3 of Feast]; "Glory...": of Triodion; "Both now and ever...": of Feast; Little Entrance, Prokeimenon, Old Testament Readings; Aposticha: Resurrectional Stichira, "Glory...": of Triodion, "Both now and ever...": of Feast...).

[^255]: Feast of the Meeting of our Lord Jesus Christ (Hypapante, February 2) — Situation II Conclusion (§§ 12–13) and Sunday After the Feast Within the Triodion (§ 12 concl.): Detailed epigraphic synthesis of physical leaf p391 (printed page 376) and facing English leaf p392 (printed page 377). Paragraph 12 completes the rubrical order for Sunday Matins when February 2 falls on a Sunday within the pre-Lenten Triodion period (Publican and Pharisee, Prodigal Son, Meatfare, or Cheesefare). Following the Triadic Canon and festal Litiya (with Triodion Doxastikon when appointed), the Hexapsalmos and "God is the Lord" (*Θεὸς Κύριος*) lead into the distribution of Kathismata across three Stichologiai: Resurrectional Kathismata combined with festal Kathismata *Χορὸς Ἀγγελικός* and *Ὁ ὢν σὺν τῷ Πατρί*, while the third festal Kathisma *Νηπιάζει δι’ ἐμέ* is sung twice. After the Hypakoe and Anavathmoi of the Tone, the Prokeimenon (Psalm 44:18 LXX) and festal Liturgy Gospel are proclaimed. The Canons of the Resurrection, Triodion, and Feast are chanted; after Ode 3, the Resurrectional Kontakion/Ikos and Kathismata; after Ode 6, Triodion Kontakion/Ikos, festal Menologion, and Triodion Synaxarion [Hypomnema]. Praises combine 4 Resurrectional and 4 festal Stichira (modified to 3 Resurrectional, 2 Triodion, and 3 Feast on Meatfare and Cheesefare Sundays). Paragraph 13 establishes the Divine Liturgy order: festal Antiphons from Psalm 44 LXX with the Christological refrain *Σῶσον ἡμᾶς, Υἱὲ Θεοῦ, ὁ ἐν ἀγκάλαις τοῦ Δικαίου Συμεὼν βασταχθείς...* and Sunday Little Entrance Introit Psalm 97:2 LXX (*Ἐγνώρισε Κύριος* with *ὁ ἀναστὰς ἐκ νεκρῶν*); Dismissal Troparion *Χαῖρε κεχαριτωμένη*, Kontakion *Ὁ μήτραν παρθενικήν*, festal Epistle and Sunday Gospel, Ode 9 Megalynarion, Communion Verse Psalm 115:4 LXX, and the composite festal-resurrectional Dismissal.

[^257]: Apodosis of the Feast on a Sunday Within the Triodion (§§ 17–18) and Situation III: Concurrence with the Saturday of Souls (§ 19): Detailed epigraphic synthesis of physical leaf p395 (printed page 380) and facing English leaf p396 (printed page 381). Paragraph 17 completes Sunday Matins for the festal Apodosis within the Triodion: after Psalm 50 LXX, Triadic Canon, and Triodion Litiya Idiomelon (if present), Kathismata across three Stichologiai (Resurrectional paired with festal); Canons of Resurrection, Triodion, and Feast; after Ode 3, Resurrectional Kontakion, Triodion and festal Kathismata; after Ode 6, Triodion Kontakion/Ikos and Menologion; Katavasiai *Χέρσον ἀβυσσοτόκον*, festal Megalynaria of Ode 9 (*Ἀκατάληπτόν ἐστι*) with Troparia and Katavasia *Θεοτόκε ἡ ἐλπίς. . . Ἐν νόμῳ, σκιᾷ*; Praises with 4 Resurrectional, 2 Triodion, and 3 festal Stichira; "Glory...": Triodion, "Both now and ever...": Feast (*Ὁ ἐν χερσὶ πρεσβυτικαῖς*). Paragraph 19 resolves Situation III: when the Feast of the Meeting coincides with Meatfare Saturday (the Saturday of Souls): the ancestral rubrics of the ancient Typika and the authoritative rulings of Patriarchs Constantios I (1830–1834) and Gregory VI (1835–1840, 1867–1871) mandate that the entire Office of the Souls be transferred to the preceding Saturday (the Saturday before the Sunday of the Prodigal Son), so that the Feast of the Meeting may be celebrated on its own day without displacement or abbreviation according to the primary rubrics of §§ 1–3.

[^258]: Variable Calendrical Cases for the Apodosis of the Meeting (Cases 1–5) and Cheesefare Sunday Evening Vespers (§ 20 incipit): Detailed epigraphic synthesis of physical leaf p397 (printed page 382) and facing English leaf p398 (printed page 383). The Typikon provides a rigorous 5-case combinatorial matrix for fixing the date of the Apodosis of the Meeting based upon its interaction with the movable pre-Lenten Triodion cycle: Case 1 [α΄]: Feast occurs between Sunday of Publican and Pharisee and Friday of that week -> Apodosis on regular 8th day (February 9); Case 2 [β΄]: Feast occurs between Saturday eve of Prodigal Son and Tuesday of Meatfare Week -> Apodosis celebrated early on Friday before the Saturday of Souls, because the ancestral Office of the Dead on Meatfare Saturday is inviolable and cannot be displaced for an Apodosis; Case 3 [γ΄]: Feast occurs between Wednesday of Meatfare Week and Saturday of Souls -> Apodosis postponed to Tuesday of Cheesefare Week; Case 4 [δ΄]: Feast occurs between Meatfare Sunday and Tuesday of Cheesefare Week -> Apodosis on Friday of Cheesefare Week; Case 5 [ε΄]: Feast occurs between Wednesday and Saturday of Cheesefare Week -> Apodosis celebrated on Cheesefare Sunday per §§ 16–18. When the Feast itself falls on Cheesefare Sunday (celebrated per §§ 11–13), the Apodosis is celebrated that same evening at Forgiveness Vespers (§ 20): "Lord, I have cried" combines 3 Stichira of the Feast and 3 of the Righteous Symeon; Great Prokeimenon *Μὴ ἀποστρέψῃς* (Psalm 68:18 LXX); Aposticha Idiomelon *Ἔλαμψεν ἡ χάρις σου* and festal Theotokion; proper festal Dismissal followed immediately by the Forgiveness rite without the customary priestly blessing *Δι’ εὐχῶν*.

[^259]: Cheesefare Sunday Evening Forgiveness Vespers Conclusion (§ 20 concl.) and Situation IV: Clean Monday Concurrence (§§ 21–22): Detailed epigraphic synthesis of physical leaf p399 (printed page 384) and facing English leaf p400 (printed page 385). Paragraph 20 concludes the Forgiveness Vespers rite marking the opening of Great Lent: following the festal Dismissal of the Meeting (omitting *Δι’ εὐχῶν*), the Choirs chant the penitential Troparion *Θεοτόκε Παρθένε*, 40 *Κύριε ἐλέησον*, *Ὁ ὢν εὐλογητός*, the Prayer of Saint Ephrem with Great Prostrations [Metanias], the Deacon/Priest litany *Εὐξώμεθα ὑπὲρ εἰρήνης τοῦ κόσμου*, and the hymn *Πάντων προστατεύεις* while clergy and faithful exchange the kiss of peace and mutual forgiveness, formally concluding the Apodosis of the Feast. Paragraphs 21–22 formulate Situation IV: when February 2 coincides with Clean Monday (the first day of Great Lent): on Cheesefare Sunday evening at Vespers (§ 21), "Lord, I have cried" combines 3 Triodion fasting Idiomela (*Ἐγκρατείᾳ τὴν σάρκα*) and 3 festal Stichira (*Λέγε Συμεών*), Great Prokeimenon Psalm 133:1 LXX (*Ἰδοὺ δὴ εὐλογεῖτε τὸν Κύριον*), Old Testament Readings of the Feast, and festal Aposticha; on Clean Monday at Matins (§ 22), the festal Litiya and "God is the Lord" lead into Kathismata across three Stichologiai combining Triodion fasting hymns (*Τῆς νηστείας τῇ θείᾳ ἀπαρχῇ*, *Τὴν πάνσεπτον ἐγκράτειαν*) with festal Kathismata; Anavathmoi (Antiphon 1 of Tone 4), Prokeimenon (Psalm 44:18 LXX), and festal Morning Gospel; Canon to 6 with festal Megalynaria of Ode 9 (*Ἀκατάληπτόν ἐστι*) and festal Exapostilarion *Ἐν πνεύματι τῷ Ἱερῷ* thrice; Praises combining festal Stichira Prosomia *Νόμον τὸν ἐν γράμματι* and festal Doxastikon *Ὁ ἐν χερσὶ πρεσβυτικαῖς*, concluding with the Great Doxology.

[^260]: Feast of the Meeting of our Lord Jesus Christ (February 2) — Clean Monday Liturgy Conclusion (§ 23), Apodosis of the Meeting (§ 24), and February 10: Holy Hieromartyr Charalampos (Heading & Situation I, § 1): Detailed epigraphic synthesis of physical leaf p401 (printed page 386) and facing English leaf p402 (printed page 387). Paragraph 23 completes the rubrical order for the Divine Liturgy of St. John Chrysostom when the Meeting coincides with Clean Monday (the first day of Great Lent): festal Antiphons from Psalm 44 LXX, Entrance Hymn Psalm 97:2 LXX, Dismissal Troparion *Χαῖρε κεχαριτωμένη*, Kontakion *Ὁ μήτραν παρθενικήν*, festal Epistle and Gospel, Ode 9 Megalynarion *Θεοτόκε ἡ ἐλπίς . . . Paragraph 24 establishes the Apodosis of the Meeting on Clean Monday evening: Vespers is chanted without variation per § 1, omitting Old Testament Readings; Dismissal Troparion thrice, Dismissal, and formal Apodosis; Great Compline is omitted out of festal reverence, replaced by Small Compline recited in cells in city churches, while monasteries observe their founder Typika (per Patriarchs Constantios I and Gregory VI). The general occurrence rule notes the Meeting may fall between the Sunday of the Publican and Pharisee and Clean Monday per the 34 Paschalia table. Commemoration of February 10 (Holy Hieromartyr Charalampos) begins with Situation I (§ 1): occurrence on any weekday from the beginning of the Triodion through Cheesefare Friday is governed entirely by the Menaion; Matins Katavasiai *Ἀνοίξω τὸ στόμα μου*; Liturgy Kontakion *Προστασία τῶν Χριστιανῶν*.

[^261]: February 10: Holy Hieromartyr Charalampos — Situation II: Concurrence on Sunday Outside the Triodion (§ 2) and Situation III: Concurrence on First Four Sundays of the Triodion (§§ 3–4, § 5 incipit): Detailed epigraphic synthesis of physical leaf p403 (printed page 388) and facing English leaf p404 (printed page 389). Paragraph 2 governs Situation II when February 10 falls on a Sunday outside the Triodion cycle: the Saint's Office is combined with the Resurrectional Office as customary for ranked feasts on Sundays; Praises Doxastikon is the Eothinon Gospel Sticheron; Epistle of the Saint, Gospel of the Sunday; Kontakion *Προστασία τῶν Χριστιανῶν*; Communion Verse Psalm 148:1 LXX (*Αἰνεῖτε*). Paragraphs 3–5 govern Situation III when the feast occurs on one of the first four Sundays of the Triodion (Publican and Pharisee, Prodigal Son, Meatfare, or Cheesefare): on Saturday evening at Great Vespers (§ 3), 10 Stichira at "Lord, I have cried" combine 4 Resurrectional, 3 Triodion, and 3 of the Saint; Doxastikon of the Triodion, first Dogmatic Theotokion of the Tone; Old Testament Readings of the Saint; Aposticha Resurrectional with Doxastikon of the Saint and Theotokion of the Triodion; Dismissal Troparia of Resurrection, Saint, and Theotokion. On Sunday at Matins (§ 4): after Psalm 50 LXX, Triadic Canon, festal Litiya of the Saint, Hexapsalmos, and "God is the Lord"; Psalter and Polyeleos; Resurrectional Kathismata with 3rd Kathisma of the Saint; Evlogitaria, Hypakoe, Anavathmoi of the Tone, Prokeimenon; Canons of Resurrection, Triodion, and Saint; after Ode 3, Resurrectional Kontakion/Ikos and Kathismata of the Saint, Triodion, and Theotokion; after Ode 6, Triodion Kontakion/Ikos, Menologion of the Saint, and Sunday Synaxarion; Triodion Katavasiai; Eothinon Gospel sequence; *Τὴν τιμιωτέραν*; Exapostilaria of Resurrection, Triodion, Saint, and Theotokion; Praises with 3 Resurrectional, 2 Triodion, and 3 Saint Stichira; Triodion Doxastikon, *Ὑπερευλογημένη*, Great Doxology, and *Σήμερον σωτηρία*. Paragraph 5 begins the Divine Liturgy order with Typika and Beatitudes (4 of Tone, 4 of Ode 6 of Triodion Canon).

[^262]: February 10: Holy Hieromartyr Charalampos — Situation III Divine Liturgy Conclusion (§ 5 concl.) and Situation IV: Anticipated Celebration on Friday Before Saturday of Souls (§§ 6–7, § 8 incipit): Detailed epigraphic synthesis of physical leaf p405 (printed page 390) and facing English leaf p406 (printed page 391). Paragraph 5 concludes the Divine Liturgy for Situation III: following the Little Entrance, Troparia of the Resurrection, the Saint, the Temple Patron, and Triodion Kontakion; Epistle of the Saint, Sunday Gospel; *Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*; Communion Verse Psalm 148:1 LXX (*Αἰνεῖτε*), and Dismissal. Paragraphs 6–8 resolve Situation IV when February 10 coincides with Meatfare Saturday (Saturday of Souls): the commemoration of St. Charalampos is anticipated and celebrated on Friday together with the Apodosis of the Meeting so as not to displace the ancestral Office of the Dead. On Thursday evening at Great Vespers (§ 6): at "Lord, I have cried", 3 festal Idiomela of the Meeting and 3 Prosomia of the Saint; Doxastikon of the Saint, festal Theotokion; Old Testament Readings of the Saint; Aposticha festal Idiomela with Doxastikon of the Saint and festal Theotokion; Dismissal Troparia of the Feast, the Saint, and the Feast again. On Friday at Matins (§ 7): after Psalm 50 LXX, Litiya of the Saint, Trisagion, festal Troparion, and Hexapsalmos; "God is the Lord" with Troparia as at Vespers; Psalter and Polyeleos of the Saint; Kathismata of the Saint with festal Kathismata in place of Theotokia; Anavathmoi (Antiphon 1 of Tone 4), Prokeimenon Psalm 91:13 LXX (*Δίκαιος ὡς φοῖνιξ*), festal Morning Gospel; Psalm 50 LXX, *Ταῖς τοῦ Ἀθλοφόρου* ("Through the intercessions of the prize-bearing champion"), Idiomelon *Φάλαγγα θεοστεφῆ*; Canons of Feast and Saint; Kathismata after Ode 3; Kontakion/Ikos and Menologion of the Saint after Ode 6; Katavasiai *Χέρσον ἀβυσσοτόκον* and Ode 9 Megalynaria of the Meeting (*Ἀκατάληπτόν ἐστι*); Exapostilaria of Feast, Saint, and Feast; Praises (3 Feast, 3 Saint), Doxastikon of the Saint, festal Theotokion, Great Doxology, and festal Dismissal Troparion. Paragraph 8 opens the Divine Liturgy with festal Antiphons and Entrance Hymn Psalm 97:2 LXX (*Ἐγνώρισε Κύριος*).

[^263]: February 10: Holy Hieromartyr Charalampos — Situation IV Divine Liturgy Conclusion (§ 8 concl.), Situation V: Cheesefare Wednesday or Friday (§ 9), and Situation VI: Saturday of Cheesefare (§§ 10–11): Detailed epigraphic synthesis of physical leaf p407 (printed page 392) and facing English leaf p408 (printed page 393). Paragraph 8 concludes the anticipated Friday Liturgy: festal Ode 9 Megalynarion (*Θεοτόκε ἡ ἐλπίς . . . Ἐν νόμῳ σκιᾷ*), Communion Verse Psalm 115:4 LXX (*Ποτήριον σωτηρίου*); on Friday evening and Saturday morning, the Office of the Souls is chanted without interruption per the Triodion. Paragraph 9 establishes Situation V when February 10 occurs on Wednesday or Friday of Cheesefare Week: celebrated entirely per the Menaion without Triodion fasting Idiomela; Divine Liturgy of St. John Chrysostom is celebrated; Epistle and Gospel of the Saint; Katavasiai *Ἀνοίξω τὸ στόμα μου*; Kontakion *Προστασία τῶν Χριστιανῶν*. Paragraphs 10–11 govern Situation VI when February 10 coincides with Cheesefare Saturday (Commemoration of the Holy Ascetic Monks and Nuns): on Friday evening at Great Vespers (§ 10), at "Lord, I have cried", 3 Prosomia of the Saint and 3 of the Venerable Fathers; Doxastikon of the Saint (*Ἔθυσας τῷ Θεῷ*), Dogmatic Theotokion *Ὁ διὰ σὲ Θεοπάτωρ*; Old Testament Readings of the Saint; Aposticha Prosomia of the Saint with Doxastikon of the Fathers and Theotokion *Δέσποινα πρόσδεξαι*; Dismissal Troparia of the Saint, the Venerable Fathers, and Theotokion. On Saturday at Matins (§ 11): Morning Gospel of the Saint; Canons of the Theotokos (*Ὑγρὰν διοδεύσας*), the Saint, and the Venerable Fathers; Katavasiai *Ἀνοίξω τὸ στόμα μου*; Exapostilaria of the Saint, the Fathers, and Theotokion; Praises (3 Saint, 3 Fathers), Doxastikon of the Saint (*Ὥσπερ ἀλάβαστρον πλῆρες*), Theotokion *Μακαρίζομέν σε*, Great Doxology, Dismissal Troparion of the Saint; Divine Liturgy of St. John Chrysostom with Kontakion *Προστασία τῶν Χριστιανῶν*, Epistle of the Saint, Gospel of the Fathers, and Communion Verse Psalm 111:6 LXX (*Εἰς μνημόσυνον αἰώνιον*).

[^264]: February 10: Holy Hieromartyr Charalampos — Situation VII: Concurrence on Clean Monday (§ 12) and Situation VIII: Concurrence on Tuesday of First Week (§§ 13–14 incipit): Detailed epigraphic synthesis of physical leaf p409 (printed page 394) and facing English leaf p410 (printed page 395). Paragraph 12 governs Situation VII when February 10 falls on Clean Monday (first day of Great Lent): the entire Office of the Saint is transferred and celebrated on Cheesefare Sunday according to the order set forth in §§ 3–5. Paragraphs 13–14 inaugurate Situation VIII when February 10 falls on Tuesday of the First Week of Great Lent: on Monday morning at Vespers (§ 13), at "Lord, I have cried", 3 Triodion Prosomia and 3 of the Saint to melodic model *Ἔδωκας σημείωσιν* ("Thou hast given a sign", Tone 4); Doxastikon and Theotokion Prosomia; "O Gladsome Light" and Triodion Old Testament Readings of the day; Aposticha fasting Idiomelon twice with Martyrikon; Dismissal Troparia *Θεοτόκε Παρθένε* with prostrations. On Monday evening at Great Compline (§ 13 concl.): at the solemn choral Verses of *Παναγία Δέσποινα Θεοτόκε*, the proper petition for St. Charalampos is inserted after that of the Temple Patron: "O holy, glorious Hieromartyr and Wonderworker Charalampos, intercede for us sinners." On Tuesday at Matins (§ 14 incipit): Triodion material is suppressed; after Psalm 50 LXX, Litiya of the Saint, Trisagion, Troparion, and Hexapsalmos; "God is the Lord" with Troparion of the Saint twice and Theotokion; Psalter and Polyeleos; Kathismata with Theotokia; Anavathmoi (Antiphon 1 of Tone 4), Prokeimenon Psalm 91:13 LXX (*Δίκαιος ὡς φοῖνιξ*), Morning Gospel; Psalm 50 LXX, *Ταῖς τοῦ Ἀθλοφόρου* ("Through the intercessions of the prize-bearing champion"), Idiomelon *Φάλαγγα θεοστεφῆ*; Canons of the Theotokos (*Ὑγρὰν διοδεύσας*) and the Saint; Kathisma and Theotokion after Ode 3; Kontakion/Ikos and Menologion after Ode 6; Katavasiai *Ἀνοίξω τὸ στόμα μου*; *Τὴν τιμιωτέραν*; Exapostilaria of the Saint and Theotokion (text breaks at the Praises, continuing directly onto leaf p411 in Cohort 42).

## Cohort 43 Footnotes

[^270]: February 24: First and Second Finding of the Precious Head of the Forerunner — Situations I through V (§§ 1–5): Detailed epigraphic synthesis of physical leaf p421 (printed page 406) and facing English leaf p422 (printed page 407). Paragraph 1 establishes Situation I: when February 24 falls on any weekday (Monday through Saturday) between Thursday of the Week of the Prodigal Son and Friday of Cheesefare Week, the service is chanted entirely as set forth in the Menaion. Paragraph 2 governs Situation II: when the feast concurs with the Saturday of Souls (Meatfare Saturday, the universal commemoration of all deceased Orthodox Christians), the service of the Forerunner is transferred and chanted in advance on Friday alongside the commemoration of the Holy Hieromartyr Polycarp of Smyrna (February 23), whereas the Saturday of Souls remains immoveable on Saturday. Paragraph 3 governs Situation III: when the feast falls on Meatfare Sunday or Cheesefare Sunday, the order of service conforms exactly to the typikon rubrics governing the commemoration of the Holy Hieromartyr Charalampos (February 10) under Situation Three, Paragraphs 3, 4, and 5 (combining Resurrectional hymns, Triodion propers, and feast hymns). Paragraph 4 governs Situation IV: when the feast falls on Cheesefare Saturday (the commemoration of all the Holy Ascetic Fathers and Mothers), the service follows the order of St. Charalampos under Situation Six, Paragraphs 10 and 11. Paragraph 5 governs Situation V: when February 24 falls on Clean Monday (the first day of the Great Fast), the service of the Forerunner cannot be celebrated on a strict Lenten aliturgical day and is chanted in advance on Cheesefare Sunday according to the order of St. Charalampos under Situation Three, Paragraphs 3, 4, and 5.

[^271]: February 24: First and Second Finding of the Precious Head of the Forerunner — Situation VI: Concurrence on Tuesday of the First Week of Great Lent (§§ 6–8): Detailed epigraphic synthesis of physical leaf p423 (printed page 408) and facing English leaf p424 (printed page 409). Paragraph 6 details the service of Vespers celebrated on Clean Monday morning: after Introductory Psalm 103 LXX, at "Lord, I have cried", 6 Stichira combine 3 cycle Prosomia from the Triodion and 3 of the Forerunner (*Χαίροις ἡ ἱερὰ κεφαλή*, "Rejoice, O sacred head"); Doxastikon and Prosomion Theotokion; "O Gladsome Light", Old Testament Readings of the Triodion; at the Aposticha, the Triodion Idiomelon is chanted twice and the Martyrikon once, followed by "Glory... Both now and ever...", Theotokion, "Now lettest Thou Thy servant depart" (Luke 2:29), Trisagion Prayers, the kneeling troparion *Θεοτόκε Παρθένε* ("O Virgin Theotokos"), and Dismissal. Paragraph 7 details Tuesday Matins and the Hours: after the Hexapsalmos, at "God is the Lord", the Dismissal Troparion of the Forerunner *Ἐκ γῆς ἀνατείλασα* ("Having arisen from the earth", Tone 4) is chanted twice, followed by the Theotokion; Psalter and Kathismata in order; Anavathmoi (Tone 4, First Antiphon); Prokeimenon Psalm 131:17 LXX (*Ἐκεῖ ἐξανατελῶ κέρας τῷ Δαβίδ*); "Let every breath praise the Lord" and the Morning Gospel (Luke 7:17–30); Psalm 50 LXX read plainly, *Ταῖς τοῦ σοῦ Προδρόμου* ("Through the intercessions of Thy Forerunner"), *Ταῖς τῆς Θεοτόκου*, Psalm 50:3 LXX, and the Idiomelon *Ἡ τῶν θείων ἐννοιῶν* ("The divine treasure"); Canons: the Theotokos Canon *Ὑγρὰν διοδεύσας* and the Canon of the Forerunner; Katavasiai *Ἀνοίξω τὸ στόμα μου*; after "More honorable than the Cherubim", the Exapostilarion of the Forerunner and Theotokion; at the Praises, 4 Prosomia *Ἤνοιξε Προπύλαια* ("He opened the fore-doors"), Doxastikon *Τὴν πανσεβάσμιον κάραν* ("The all-venerable head"), Theotokion *Θεοτόκε σὺ εἶ ἡ ἄμπελος* ("O Theotokos, thou art the true vine"), Great Doxology, and Dismissal Troparion; plain Hours are read with the Troparion and Kontakion *Προφῆτα Θεοῦ καὶ Πρόδρομε* ("O Prophet of God and Forerunner"); at the Ninth Hour, the Beatitudes and penitential troparia are chanted per St. Charalampos Situation Eight, Paragraph 14. Paragraph 8 details the Divine Liturgy of the Presanctified Gifts celebrated on Tuesday: at Vespers, Kathisma 18 (Psalms 119–133 LXX), 10 Stichira at "Lord, I have cried" (Triodion Aposticha Idiomelon twice, Martyrikon, 3 Triodion Prosomia, 4 Forerunner *Δεῦτε τὴν τιμίαν κεφαλήν*, "Come, let us honor the precious head"), Doxastikon *Ἡ τῶν θείων ἐννοιῶν*, Stavrotheotokion; Little Entrance with the Gospel Book, "O Gladsome Light", Triodion Readings, *Κατευθυνθήτω* (Psalm 140:2 LXX), Epistle 2 Corinthians 4:6–15, Gospel Matthew 11:2–15, *Νῦν αἱ δυνάμεις*, Communion Verse Psalm 111:6 LXX (*Εἰς μνημόσυνον*), Psalm 33:2 LXX, and Dismissal.

[^272]: February 24: First and Second Finding of the Precious Head of the Forerunner — Situations VII and VIII (§§ 9–11): Detailed epigraphic synthesis of physical leaf p425 (printed page 410) and facing English leaf p426 (printed page 411). Paragraph 9 governs Situation VII: when February 24 falls on Wednesday, Thursday, or Friday of the First Week of Great Lent, the typikon order follows the model of St. Charalampos under Situations Nine and Eleven, Paragraphs 16 and 18 (the printed Greek text exhibits a numerical reference citation to §§ 12 and 16, which corresponds structurally to the respective Wednesday and Friday rubrics of the St. Charalampos section). Paragraph 10 governs Situation VIII: when the feast falls on Saturday of the First Week of Great Lent (Theodore Saturday, commemorating the Miracle of the Kolyva wrought by the Great Martyr Theodore the Recruit): on Friday morning at Vespers, 10 Stichira at "Lord, I have cried" combine the day's Idiomelon *Δεῦτε πιστοὶ ἐπεργασώμεθα* ("Come, ye faithful, let us work", twice), 4 Prosomia of the Forerunner, and 4 of St. Theodore; Doxastikon of St. Theodore *Ὀργάνῳ χρησάμενος* ("Using the apostate emperor as his tool"), and the first Dogmatic Theotokion of the Tone occurring; Little Entrance with the censer, "O Gladsome Light", Old Testament Readings of the Triodion, *Κατευθυνθήτω*, *Νῦν αἱ δυνάμεις*, Communion Verse Psalm 33:9 LXX (*Γεύσασθε καὶ ἴδετε*, "O taste and see"), Psalm 33:2 LXX, and Dismissal. Paragraph 11 details Saturday Matins and the Divine Liturgy of St. John Chrysostom: after the Midnight Office and Hexapsalmos, "God is the Lord" with Dismissal Troparia of the Forerunner, St. Theodore (*Μεγάλα τὰ τῆς πίστεως*), and Theotokion; Kathismata of both Saints; Tone 4 Anavathmoi (Antiphon 1); Prokeimenon Psalm 131:17 LXX; Morning Gospel of the Forerunner (Luke 7:17–30); Psalm 50 LXX, *Ταῖς τοῦ σοῦ Προδρόμου*, *Ταῖς τῆς Θεοτόκου*, Psalm 50:3 LXX, and Idiomelon *Ἡ τῶν θείων ἐννοιῶν*; Canons: Triodion Ode 1 and Forerunner; after Ode 3, Kontakion and Ikos of the Forerunner, and Kathismata of the Menaion and Triodion with Theotokia; after Ode 6, Kontakion and Ikos of the Triodion, Menologion of the Forerunner, and Synaxarion of the Triodion; Katavasiai *Ἀνοίξω τὸ στόμα μου*; after "More honorable than the Cherubim", Exapostilaria of the Forerunner, St. Theodore, and Theotokion; at the Praises, 3 Prosomia of the Forerunner and 3 of St. Theodore; Doxastikon of the Forerunner, Theotokion, Great Doxology, and Dismissal Troparion of the Forerunner; Divine Liturgy of St. John Chrysostom with Kontakion *Προστασία τῶν χριστιανῶν*, Epistle of the Triodion (Hebrews 1:1–12), Gospel of the Forerunner (Matthew 11:2–15), Communion Verse Psalm 111:6 LXX (*Εἰς μνημόσυνον*), and Dismissal.

[^273]: February 24: First and Second Finding of the Precious Head of the Forerunner — Situation IX and Situation X Opening (§§ 12–14): Detailed epigraphic synthesis of physical leaf p427 (printed page 412) and facing English leaf p428 (printed page 413). Paragraph 12 governs Situation IX: when February 24 concurs with the First Sunday of Great Lent (Sunday of Orthodoxy), the order follows the rubrics for St. Charalampos under Situation Thirteen, Paragraphs 23–25. Footnote 2 of the Greek source text notes an important historical witness: the Typikon of the Great Church compiled under Emperor Constantine VII Porphyrogenitus (*Τὸ τοῦ Κωνσταντίνου Τυπικὸν*) transfers the feast of the Forerunner to the Saturday of the Second Week of Great Lent (falling on March 1 or 2 in that calendar configuration) to prevent overshadowing the Sunday of Orthodoxy. Paragraph 13 establishes Situation X: when February 24 falls on the Second Sunday of Great Lent (commemoration of St. Gregory Palamas, Archbishop of Thessalonica): on Saturday evening at Great Vespers, after Introductory Psalm 103 LXX and Kathisma 1 of the Psalter, at "Lord, I have cried", 10 Stichira combine 4 Resurrectional of the Tone, 3 of the Forerunner, and 3 of St. Gregory; Doxastikon of the Triodion, and first Dogmatic Theotokion of the Tone; Little Entrance, "O Gladsome Light", and Saturday evening Prokeimenon; at the Aposticha, the Resurrectional Stichira, Doxastikon of the Forerunner *Ἡ τῶν θείων ἐννοιῶν*, Theotokion *Ὢ θαύματος καινοῦ* ("O strange marvel"), and Dismissal Troparia of the Resurrection, the Forerunner, St. Gregory, and Theotokion. Paragraph 14 details Sunday Matins: after Psalm 50 LXX, the Triadic Canon and hymns *Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*, Trisagion Prayers, penitential troparia *Ἐλέησον ἡμᾶς*, Hexapsalmos, and "God is the Lord" with Troparia as at Vespers; Psalter and Amomos (Psalm 118 LXX); Resurrectional Kathismata, 3rd Stichologia Kathisma of the Forerunner with Theotokion; Evlogitaria, Hypakoe, Anavathmoi of the Tone, Prokeimenon; Canons of the Resurrection, the Forerunner, and St. Gregory; after Ode 3, Resurrectional Kontakion and Ikos, followed by Kathismata of the Triodion, the Forerunner, and Theotokion; after Ode 6, Kontakion and Ikos of the Triodion, Menologion of the Forerunner, and Synaxarion of the Triodion; Katavasiai *Ἀνοίξω τὸ στόμα μου*; Sunday Morning Gospel sequence; *Τὴν τιμιωτέραν*; Exapostilaria of the Resurrection, Triodion, Forerunner, St. Gregory, and Theotokion; at the Praises, 3 Resurrectional Stichira, 3 of the Forerunner, and 2 of St. Gregory; Doxastikon of the Triodion *Τοῖς ἐν σκότει ἁμαρτημάτων* ("Unto those who walk in the darkness of sins"), Theotokion *Ὑπερευλογημένη*, Great Doxology, and *Σήμερον σωτηρία*.

[^274]: February 24: First and Second Finding of the Precious Head of the Forerunner — Situation X Conclusion (§ 15), Situation XI (§ 16), Concurrence Rules (§ 17), and Festal Occurrence Envelope: Detailed epigraphic synthesis of physical leaf p429 (printed page 414) and facing English leaf p430 (printed page 415). Paragraph 15 concludes Situation X: at the Divine Liturgy of St. Basil the Great on the Second Sunday of Great Lent, Typika and Beatitudes (4 of the Tone, 4 from Ode 6 of the Triodion Canon); after the Little Entrance, Dismissal Troparia of the Resurrection, the Forerunner, St. Gregory Palamas, the Patron Saint of the Temple, and Kontakion *Τῇ ὑπερμάχῳ* ("To thee, the champion leader"); Epistle of the Forerunner and Gospel of the Sunday (Mark 2:1–12), Liturgy of St. Basil the Great, Communion Verse Psalm 148:1 LXX (*Αἰνεῖτε τὸν Κύριον*), and Dismissal. Paragraph 16 establishes Situation XI: when February 24 falls on the Third Sunday of Great Lent (Veneration of the Precious and Life-Giving Cross): on Saturday at Vespers, Kathisma 1, 10 Stichira at "Lord, I have cried" (4 Resurrectional, 3 Cross, 3 Forerunner), Doxastikon of the Triodion, first Dogmatic Theotokion of the Tone; at the Aposticha, Resurrectional Stichira, Doxastikon of the Forerunner, and Triodion Theotokion *Ὁ συμμαχήσας Κύριε* ("O Lord, Who didst aid gentle David"); Dismissal Troparia of the Resurrection, the Forerunner, and the Holy Cross (*Σῶσον Κύριε τὸν λαόν σου*, Tone 1). On Sunday morning at Matins: "God is the Lord" with Troparia as at Vespers; Kathismata in order; 3rd Stichologia Kathisma of the Forerunner and Cross Kathisma *Ἐν Παραδείσῳ μὲν τὸ πρίν*; Canons of the Triodion (Cross) and the Forerunner; after Ode 3, Resurrectional Kontakion and Ikos, and Kathismata of the Forerunner and Triodion; Exapostilaria of the Resurrection, Triodion, and Forerunner with Theotokion; at the Praises, 4 Resurrectional Stichira and 4 of the Holy Cross (the Praises of the Forerunner being omitted to preserve the primacy of the Cross veneration rite); Divine Liturgy of St. Basil the Great: after Little Entrance, Troparia of Resurrection, Cross, Forerunner, and Temple Patron; Epistle of the Forerunner and Gospel of the Sunday (Mark 8:34–9:1); Communion Verse Psalm 4:7 LXX (*Ἐσημειώθη ἐφ᾿ ἡμᾶς τὸ φῶς τοῦ προσώπου σου, Κύριε*), and Dismissal. Paragraph 17 provides the general rule for Monday occurrences during the Second, Third, or Fourth Weeks of Great Lent, directing the celebrant to St. Charalampos Situation Fourteen, Paragraphs 26 and 27, and indicating that all remaining unstated weekday occurrences likewise resolve according to the general rubrics established for St. Charalampos. The concluding rubric summarizes the liturgical occurrence envelope: according to the Paschal calculation table (Heortodromion), February 24 can fall within the Triodion season between Thursday of the Week of the Prodigal Son and Tuesday of the Fourth Week of Great Lent.

Paragraph 12 establishes Situation VII: when the feast falls on Mid-Lent Wednesday (Wednesday of the 4th Week), Matins follows Situation I, Paragraphs 2 and 3; the Hours are read plainly, replacing the standard Lenten Troparia with the veneration of the Precious Cross: "Thy Cross do we adore, O Master" (*Τὸν Σταυρόν σου Προσκυνοῦμεν Δέσποτα*), Dismissal Troparion *Τὰς ἀλγηδόνας τῶν Ἁγίων*, and Kontakion *Οὐκέτι φλογίνη ῥομφαία*; at Vespers, after Kathisma 18 of the Psalter, at "Lord, I have cried", 10 Stichira combine the 2 Idiomela and the Martyrikon, 3 Prosomia of the Triodion, and 4 of the Saints; Doxastikon *Τὴν λίμνην ὡς παράδεισον*, Theotokion *Σήμερον ὁ ἀπρόσιτος τῇ οὐσίᾳ*, Little Entrance with the Holy Gospel Book, "O Gladsome Light", Readings of the day, *Κατευθυνθήτω*, Epistle and Gospel of the Martyrs, Presanctified Liturgy with Communion Verse Psalm 111:6 LXX (*Εἰς μνημόσυνον*), and Dismissal. Paragraph 13 establishes Situation VIII: when the feast falls on Saturday of Weeks 2, 3, or 4 of Great Lent, on Friday morning at Vespers, 10 Stichira at "Lord, I have cried" combine the day's Idiomelon twice, 4 Martyrika in the Tone occurring, and 4 of the Saints; Doxastikon *Ἐν ᾠδαῖς ᾀσμάτων*, first Theotokion of the Tone, Little Entrance with the censer, "O Gladsome Light", Readings, *Κατευθυνθήτω*, Presanctified Liturgy with Communion Verse Psalm 33:9 LXX (*Γεύσασθε καὶ ἴδετε*), and Dismissal; on Friday evening, the Oikoi of the Theotokos (Akathist Stasis) are read as customary, with Kontakion *Πᾶσαν στρατιάν*.

[^284]: March 9: Commemoration of the Holy Forty Martyrs of Sebastea — Situation XII Conclusion (§ 21, Festal Range Note); March 25: The Annunciation of the Most Holy Theotokos — Paramony Rubric and Situation I Opening (§ 1). Detailed epigraphic synthesis of physical leaf p449 (printed page 434) and facing English leaf p450 (printed page 435). Paragraph 21 concludes Situation XII: at the Divine Liturgy of St. John Chrysostom, Typika and Beatitudes appoint 4 troparia from Ode 3 of the Theotokos and 4 from Ode 6 of the Saints; at the Little Entrance, the Third Antiphon refrain is chanted: "O come, let us worship and bow down before Christ; save us, O Son of God, wondrous art Thou in the Saints, who sing to Thee: Alleluia", followed by Troparion *Τὸ προσταχθὲν μυστικῶς*, that of the Saints, the Temple Patron, and Kontakion *Τῇ ὑπερμάχῳ*; Epistle of the Saints and Gospel *Ἀναστᾶσα Μαριάμ* (Luke 1:39–49, 56); Megalynarion at "Especially": *Ἅπας γηγενής*; Communion Verse: Psalm 115:4 LXX (*Ποτήριον σωτηρίου*); *Εἴδομεν τὸ φῶς*, and Dismissal. The general rubric notes that the Feast of the Forty Martyrs can fall within the Triodion cycle between Wednesday of the First Week of Great Lent and Great and Holy Monday of Passion Week. For March 25 (The Annunciation of the Most Holy Theotokos), the Paramony Rubric distinguishes cathedral/parish usage from monastic typika: when the Eve falls on Wednesday or Friday, parish churches do not celebrate the Presanctified Liturgy because they do not hold an all-night vigil (except on Great and Holy Tuesday and Wednesday), whereas monasteries celebrate the Presanctified Liturgy combined with Small Vespers according to ancient founder typika. Paragraph 1 establishes Situation I: when the Annunciation falls on Friday of the 3rd Week of Great Lent, on Wednesday morning at Vespers of the Presanctified, after Kathisma 18, at "Lord, I have cried", 10 Stichira combine the day's Idiomelon twice, Martyrikon once, 3 Prosomia of the sequence of the Triodion, and 4 Forefeast Prosomia *Κεκρυμμένον μυστήριον*; Doxastikon *Εὐαγγελίζεται ὁ Γαβριὴλ*, Little Entrance with "O Gladsome Light", Readings of the day, *Κατευθυνθήτω*, and the Liturgy of the Presanctified Gifts follows in due order.

Paragraph 69 introduces Situation XXIII: concurrence on Holy and Great Friday or Holy and Great Saturday: the Feast is transferred and celebrated on Easter Sunday itself together with the Resurrection Office. Violakis transcribes the canonical decree of the Ecumenical Patriarchate: "The Holy and Great Church of Christ, having received this tradition from Patriarchs and Hierarchs from a century ago to the present, observing the disagreement and confusion occurring throughout all the churches in cities and villages, took thought especially concerning the great solemnity of the Annunciation. And indeed, for the cessation of the apparent anomaly, especially in the ears of the simple folk who do not perceive deeply the things of the Spirit, the Church ordained that, if the Feast falls on these two sorrowful days [Holy Friday or Holy Saturday], it should be transferred to the supreme day of Pascha itself named after the Lord. In order that joyous things may be sung and melodized together with joyous things, the Church by economy prevented the mixing of the bright with the sorrowful, in order also that no disharmony might be shown between: 'Today He is hung upon the tree' (*Σήμερον κρεμᾶται ἐπὶ ξύλου*) and: 'Today are the glad tidings of joy' (*Σήμερον χαρᾶς εὐαγγέλια*), and between: 'Pouring out tears of lamentation over Thee, O Pure One' (*Δακρυρρόους θρήνους ἐπὶ σὲ Ἁγνὴ*) and: 'Gabriel to the Virgin the glad tidings' (*Ὁ Γαβριὴλ τῇ Παρθένῳ τὸ Εὐαγγέλιον*). But these provisions, as has been said, pertain only to the churches in cities and villages..."

Paragraph 13 details the Divine Liturgy: Antiphons of the Feast, Entrance Hymn [Eisodikon]: *Δεῦτε προσκυνήσωμεν . . . ὁ ἀναστὰς ἐκ νεκρῶν*. The rubric concludes with an explicit patriarchal epigraphic witness: "This is the order celebrated at the Great Church, where the holy relics of the Saint are kept in the Chapel of the Pammakaristos," documenting the translation of Saint Euphemia's relics preserved at the Ecumenical Patriarchate.

The Dismissal Troparia: of the Resurrection, of the Saint, the Theotokion, and Dismissal. The rubric notes that the service of Saint Ermolaos is chanted at Compline, except where the church is dedicated to the Saint. Paragraph 3 details Sunday Matins and Liturgy: the entire service is chanted as on the commemoration of Saint Kyriake (see July 7, §§ 3–4); at the Praises: 4 Resurrection Stichira and 4 of the Saint; in the Divine Liturgy: Epistle of the Saint and Gospel of the Sunday; *Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*; Communion Hymn: *Αἰνεῖτε* [Ps. 148:1 LXX], etc. Commemoration of July 27: The Holy Great-Martyr and Healer Panteleimon: Paragraph 1 begins weekday occurrence: if the commemoration occurs on any other day except Sunday, the service is chanted according to the Menaion.

Concluding Special Rubric: If July 31 falls on a Sunday, the service of the Forefeast of the Procession of the Precious Cross is omitted in the parish churches of the cities, as there is no Forefeast Canon appointed in Matins; the ancient typika of the monasteries, however, continue to be observed according to their customary rule.
