Commemoration of August 2: Translation of the Relics of Saint Stephen: Paragraph 1 concludes: Aposticha Verses: *Δίκαιος ὡς φοῖνιξ ἀνθήσει* [Ps. 91:13 LXX] and *Πεφυτευμένος ἐν τῷ οἴκῳ Κυρίου* [Ps. 91:14 LXX]; "Glory...": *Χαίροις ἐν Κυρίῳ Στέφανε μακάριε*; "Both now and ever...": *Θεοτόκε σὺ εἶ ἡ ἄμπελος . . . μετὰ τοῦ Ἀθλοφόρου*; *Νῦν ἀπολύεις*, and immediately begins the Order of the Paraklesis. Section: The Order of the Paraklesis (Supplicatory Canon to the Most Holy Theotokos throughout the Dormition Fast, August 1–14): The Patriarch (or Superior) recites Psalm 142 [LXX] *Κύριε εἰσάκουσον τῆς προσευχῆς μου* in a low voice [recto tono]; the Choirs chant "God is the Lord" four times in Tone 4, with *Τῇ Θεοτόκῳ ἐκτενῶς νῦν προσδράμωμεν*; "Glory...": Dismissal Troparion of the Patron Saint of the Church; "Both now and ever...": *Οὐ σιωπήσωμέν ποτε Θεοτόκε*; Psalm 50 [LXX] is read in a low voice. Then the Canon of the Small Paraklesis is chanted without Heirmoi, beginning immediately with *Ὑπεραγία Θεοτόκε σῶσον ἡμᾶς... Πολλοῖς συνεχόμενος πειρασμοῖς*, with 4 Troparia in each Ode. After Ode 3: *Διάσωσον ἀπὸ κινδύνων* and *Ἐπίβλεψον ἐν εὐμενείᾳ*; the Priest intones the Litany: *Ἐλέησον ἡμᾶς ὁ Θεός*, with Choirs chanting *Κύριε ἐλέησον* 12 times (4 sets of 3); Sessional Hymn: *Πρεσβεία θερμή*, and the Second Choir begins Ode 4. After Ode 6: *Διάσωσον ἀπὸ κινδύνων* and *Ἄχραντε ἡ διὰ λόγου*; the Priest intones the Insistent Litany: *Ἐλέησον ἡμᾶς ὁ Θεός*; Kontakion: *Προστασία τῶν χριστιανῶν*; Prokeimenon: *Μνησθήσομαι τοῦ ὀνόματός σου* [Ps. 44:18 LXX]; *Πᾶσα πνοή*, and Gospel of the Mother of God: *Ἀναστᾶσα Μαριάμ* (Luke 1:39–49, 56); "Glory...": *Πάτερ, Λόγε, Πνεῦμα*; "Both now and ever...": *Ταῖς τῆς Θεοτόκου*; Psalm 50 verse: *Ἐλέησόν με ὁ Θεός*, and the Sticheron: *Μὴ καταπιστεύσῃς με ἀνθρωπίνῃ προστασίᾳ*, *Οὐδεὶς προστρέχων ἐπὶ σοί*, *Μεταβολὴ τῶν θλιβομένων*. Priest proclaims: *Σῶσον ὁ Θεὸς τὸν λαόν σου*; Choirs sing *Κύριε ἐλέησον* 12 times; Prayer: *Ἐλέει καὶ οἰκτιρμοῖς*; Odes 7, 8, and 9 are chanted. After Ode 9: Megalynaria: *Ἄξιόν ἐστιν ὡς ἀληθῶς*, *Τὴν Ὑψηλοτέραν τῶν οὐρανῶν*, etc. During *Ἄλαλα τὰ χείλη τῶν ἀσεβῶν*, the Patriarch venerates the icon of the Theotokos and, returning to the Throne, blesses the people while the Choirs chant *Εἰς πολλὰ ἔτη*; then the remaining Megalynaria: *Ψάλλομεν προθύμως σοι τὴν Ὠδήν*, of the Patron Saint of the Church, and *Πᾶσαι τῶν Ἀγγέλων αἱ στρατιαί*; Trisagion Prayers; Dismissal Troparion of the Saint: *Βασίλειον διάδημα*, and Theotokion: *Τὸ ἀπ᾿ αἰῶνος ἀπόκρυφον*. Priest intones the Litany: *Ἐλέησον ἡμᾶς ὁ Θεός*, *Ἔτι δεόμεθα ὑπὲρ τοῦ διαφυλαχθῆναι...*; Choirs respond *Κύριε ἐλέησον*; Patriarch proclaims: *Ἐπάκουσον ἡμῶν ὁ Θεός*; Priest: *Σοφία*.

Original Printed Footnote 1: George Violakis documents that while the printed Horologion prescribes chanting the Megalynaria *Τὴν Ὑψηλοτέραν τῶν οὐρανῶν*, etc., after the Ninth Ode, and placing the Exaposteilaria *Ἀπόστολοι ἐκ περάτων* after the Trisagion in place of Dismissal Troparia, the Patriarchal practice of Constantinople strictly maintains the order noted above (Exaposteilaria immediately after Ode 9, and Penitential Troparia after the Trisagion).

Original Printed Footnote 4: George Violakis documents the patriarchal prohibition against the unauthorized chanting of Enkomia to the Theotokos: In certain parishes, where the Feast of the Dormition is celebrated with solemnity, an unauthorized practice arose—supposedly for the greater honor of the Theotokos—of chanting so-called Enkomia [Lamentations/Praises] after the Ninth Ode in imitation of the Matins of Great and Holy Saturday. Antiphon 3: Ps. 107:2 LXX (*Ἑτοίμη ἡ καρδία μου, ὁ Θεός, ἑτοίμη ἡ καρδία μου*), Ps. 115:3 LXX (*Τί ἀνταποδώσω τῷ Κυρίῳ περὶ πάντων, ὧν ἀνταπέδωκέ μοι;*), Ps. 115:4 LXX (*Ποτήριον σωτηρίου λήψομαι καὶ τὸ ὄνομα Κυρίου ἐπικαλέσομαι*) with refrain: Dismissal Troparion: *Ἐν τῇ Γεννήσει τὴν παρθενίαν ἐφύλαξας...* After the Little Entrance, the Dismissal Troparion: *Ἐν τῇ Γεννήσει*, and the Kontakion: *Τὴν ἐν πρεσβείαις ἀκοίμητον*. The Epistle, and the Gospel...

[^388]: Month of August: The Dormition of the Most Holy Lady Theotokos (August 15, Concl. § 3, Sunday Concurrence §§ 4–6). Detailed epigraphic synthesis of physical leaf p657 (printed page 642) and facing English leaf p658 (printed page 643). Commemoration of August 15: The Dormition of our Most Holy Lady Theotokos: Paragraph 3 concludes: the Epistle [Phil. 2:5–11], and the Gospel: *Εἰσῆλθεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἰς κώμην τινά* [Luke 10:38–42; 11:27–28]. At "Especially" [Megalynarion], *Αἱ γενεαὶ πᾶσαι . . . Νενίκηνται τῆς φύσεως οἱ ὅροι*. Communion Hymn: *Ποτήριον σωτηρίου λήψομαι* [Ps. 115:4 LXX]; *Εἴδομεν τὸ φῶς*, and Dismissal. Paragraph 4 details Sunday Concurrence (if August 15 falls on a Sunday): on Saturday evening at Great Vespers following the Introductory Psalm [Ps. 103 LXX] and the Psalter reading, at "Lord, I have cried" [Ps. 140 LXX], 4 Resurrection Stichira and the Prosomoia of the Feast to 6; "Glory... Both now and ever...": *Θεαρχίῳ νεύματι*. Little Entrance, *Φῶς ἱλαρόν*, the Prokeimenon of the day, and the Readings of the Feast. At the Aposticha: the Resurrection Stichira; "Glory... Both now and ever...": *Ὅτε ἐξεδήμησας*. The Dismissal Troparia: of the Resurrection once, and of the Feast twice, and Dismissal. Paragraph 5 details Sunday Matins: after Psalm 50 [LXX], the Trinity Canon, the Litiya, and the Trinity Hymns *Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*; then the Trisagion Prayers, the Dismissal Troparion: *Ἐν τῇ Γεννήσει*, and the Six Psalms. At "God is the Lord": the Dismissal Troparia as in Vespers; then the Psalter reading and the Polyeleos: *Ἐξηρεύξατο ἡ καρδία μου* [Ps. 44 LXX]. At the Sessional Hymns of the First Stichologia: two of the Resurrection and that of the Feast: *Ἀναβόησον Δαβίδ*; at the Second Stichologia: two of the Resurrection and that of the Feast: *Ὁ πάντιμος χορός*; then the Third Sessional Hymn of the Feast twice; the Petition, the Hypakoe, the Anavathmoi of the Tone, and the Prokeimenon of the Feast: *Μνησθήσομαι τοῦ ὀνόματός σου* [Ps. 44:18 LXX]. Then *Πᾶσα πνοή*, and the Matins Gospel: *Ἀναστᾶσα Μαριάμ* [Luke 1:39–49, 56]. Then *Ἀνάστασιν Χριστοῦ θεασάμενοι*; Psalm 50 [LXX] is read in a low voice; "Glory...": *Ταῖς τῆς Θεοτόκου*; "Both now and ever...": repeat the same. The Verse: *Ἐλέησόν με ὁ Θεός* [Ps. 50:1 LXX], and the Idiomelon: *Ὅτε ἡ μετάστασις*. Then the Canons of the Resurrection and the two of the Feast. After the Third Ode, the Kontakion and Ikos of the Resurrection, and the Hypakoe: *Μακαρίζομέν σε πᾶσαι αἱ γενεαί* read in a low voice; after the Sixth Ode, the Kontakion and Ikos of the Feast, and the Menologion. The Katavasia: *Πεποικιλμένη τῇ θείᾳ δόξῃ*; then the Ninth Ode of the Feast with the Megalynaria. The Resurrection Exaposteilarion and that of the Feast twice. At the Praises: 4 hymns of the Resurrection and 4 of the Feast; "Glory... Both now and ever...": *Τῇ ἀθανάτῳ σου κοιμήσει*; Great Doxology, and *Σήμερον σωτηρία*. Paragraph 6 details the Divine Liturgy of Sunday Concurrence: the Antiphons of the Feast, and at the Second Antiphon: *Ὁ ἀναστὰς ἐκ νεκρῶν*. At the Little Entrance: *Δεῦτε προσκυνήσωμεν... ὁ ἀναστὰς ἐκ νεκρῶν*. After the Little Entrance, the Dismissal Troparia: of the Resurrection, of the Feast, and the Kontakion: *Τὴν ἐν πρεσβείαις*; the Epistle and the Gospel of the Feast. At "Especially" [Megalynarion], *Αἱ γενεαὶ πᾶσαι . . . Νενίκηνται τῆς φύσεως οἱ ὅροι*. Communion Hymn: *Ποτήριον σωτηρίου λήψομαι*...

Detailed epigraphic synthesis of physical leaf p659 (printed page 644) and facing English leaf p660 (printed page 645). Commemoration of August 15: The Dormition: Paragraph 6 concludes: Communion Hymn: *Ποτήριον σωτηρίου λήψομαι*; *Εἴδομεν τὸ φῶς*, and Dismissal. Commemoration of August 16: Translation of the Icon Not Made by Human Hands (that is, the Holy Mandylion) from Edessa; and the Holy Martyr Diomedes: Paragraph 7 details Great Vespers on the evening of August 15: following the Introductory Psalm [Ps. 103 LXX], at "Lord, I have cried" [Ps. 140 LXX], 3 Stichira Prosomoia of the Holy Mandylion, and 3 of the Feast (from Small Vespers); "Glory... Both now and ever...": *Δεῦτε τὴν παγκόσμιον κοίμησιν*. Little Entrance, *Φῶς ἱλαρόν*, and the Prokeimenon of the day. At the Aposticha: the 3 hymns of the sequence: *Δῆμος τῶν μαθητῶν*; "Glory... Both now and ever...": of the Afterfeast; Dismissal Troparia: *Τὴν ἄχραντον Εἰκόνα σου*, *Ἐν τῇ Γεννήσει*, and Dismissal. Paragraph 8 details Matins: after the Midnight Office, Psalm 50 [LXX], the Six Psalms, and the rest of the service according to the order of the Menaion. The Canon of the Feast and that of the Holy Mandylion; Katavasiai: *Πεποικιλμένη τῇ θείᾳ δόξῃ*; then *Τὴν τιμιωτέραν*; the Exaposteilarion of the sequence twice. At the Praises: the 3 Prosomoia of the Holy Mandylion from Vespers: *Ποίοις οἱ γηγενεῖς ὄμμασιν* to 4; "Glory... Both now and ever...": *Ἡ τῶν οὐρανῶν ὑψηλοτέρα* (see the Litiya); Great Doxology, and the Dismissal Troparion: *Τὴν ἄχραντον Εἰκόνα σου*. Paragraph 9 details the Divine Liturgy: the Typika and Beatitudes with 4 hymns from the Third and Sixth Odes of the Canon of the Holy Mandylion. After the Little Entrance, the Dismissal Troparia: *Τὴν ἄχραντον εἰκόνα σου*, *Ἐν τῇ Γεννήσει*, of the Patron Saint of the Church, and the Kontakion: *Τὴν ἐν πρεσβείαις*. Epistle (see Saturday before Epiphany [1 Tim. 3:13–4:5]), and the Gospel: *Τῷ καιρῷ ἐκείνῳ, ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ συμπληροῦσθαι* [Luke 9:51–56; 10:22–24]. At "Especially" [Megalynarion], *Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*; Communion Hymn: *Αἰνεῖτε τὸν Κύριον* [Ps. 148:1 LXX]; *Εἴδομεν τὸ φῶς*, and Dismissal. Paragraph 10 details Sunday Concurrence (if August 16 falls on a Sunday): on Saturday evening at Great Vespers, following the Introductory Psalm [Ps. 103 LXX] and the Psalter reading, at "Lord, I have cried" [Ps. 140 LXX], 4 Resurrection Stichira, 3 of the Holy Mandylion, and 3 of the Feast (from Small Vespers); "Glory...": *Δεῦτε φιλεόρτων τὸ σύστημα* (see the Litiya of the Feast); "Both now and ever...": the first Theotokion of the Tone. Little Entrance, *Φῶς ἱλαρόν*, and the Prokeimenon. At the Aposticha: the Resurrection Stichira; "Glory... Both now and ever...": *Ἄσατε λαοί* (see the Litiya). The Dismissal Troparia: of the Resurrection, *Τὴν ἄχραντον Εἰκόνα σου*, *Ἐν τῇ Γεννήσει*, and Dismissal. Paragraph 11 begins Sunday Matins: after Psalm 50 [LXX], the Trinity Canon and the Trinity Hymns...
